## 2026-10-09: v4 Home: eleven DiceBear avatar styles to try; the avatar picker is a dropdown

**Why:** Chandu: "From dicebear.com/animated-avatars can we have toggles and try glyphs, slice, big smile, avataaars, cameo, miniavs, constellations, plants and voxel art, voxel bot, and loops (use animated ones wherever possible). I guess our picker will have to be a dropdown now."

- The conversation cards' Portraits | Line art switch is a dropdown with 13 styles: the two house styles, then Glyphs, Slice, Big Smile, Avataaars, Cameo, Miniavs, Constellation, Sprouts (DiceBear's plants style; "plants" is not a style name), Voxel Art, Voxel Bot and Loops. The choice is remembered in the same A/B setting as before.
- Five animate (Constellation, Sprouts, Voxel Art, Voxel Bot, Loops) at DiceBear's slow speed. The animation is CSS inside the SVG, stops under prefers-reduced-motion, and needs a plain `<img>` (next/image would need dangerouslyAllowSVG).
- **Friendly faces only.** Unfiltered, Avataaars put banned parts on 56 of 60 sampled seeds (sad, screaming, vomiting mouths; crying eyes; angry brows; one demo student in a "RESIST!" shirt). Big Smile did on 45 of 60 (sad and angry faces, clown nose), Sprouts on 27 and Voxel Art on 25 (frowns, glares). Each is limited to its neutral and positive parts: 0 of 60 after filtering, and animation unaffected.
- **API gotchas** (DiceBear 10.x): options are named `<part>Variant` (the 9.x names like `mouth=` are ignored). Several comma lists in one request return 400 (FST_ERR_VALIDATION), so each value is its own repeated parameter.
- **DEMO-ONLY:** images come from the public API (api.dicebear.com, cached a year), seeded with the roster id so no student name leaves the app. For production, self-host with `@dicebear/core` and the chosen style package.
- **Square picture, five across.** Chandu, after the first pass: the avatars were "getting cropped in a few shapes when I switch them as opposed to filling the available space in the card like loops does ... not have to be a square in a square or inside another circle". The card's picture well was a wide 226x142 rectangle and every style is square art, so each one was either cropped or floated as a tile or circle inside it. The well is now square and every style fills it edge to edge (measured 176x176 for all 13). The styles drawn on a transparent canvas (Big Smile, Avataaars, Cameo, Miniavs) get DiceBear's pastel backgrounds. The portrait photos crop to the square at 20% from the top. Five cards across instead of four keeps the row close to its old height (336px, was 302px), and all five priority students show without scrolling. It is three across up to 1100px and 176px cards that scroll on phones. Pending Reviews still lines up: same card top and bottom, button bottom on the Book buttons' line (493 and 493).
- The DiceBear `<img>` is keyed on the style. A browser keeps painting an image's old picture until the new src downloads, so a switch briefly showed the previous style.

## 2026-10-09: Signal's math, sort and Power Play in the pixel theme; Power Play drag; light-mode gold

**Why:** Chandu, on the live build: "In signal that whole math thing isn't even designed in signals theme ... In light mode the tiles blend in etc and the tile that appears when dragging doesn't follow any of the pixel theme stuff. Also the font use is not consistent? Are we not using 2 fonts? Some of the text ... is small ... Also light mode amber on other pages like career details etc when it's on a darker image or background is bad, we need that same yellow-gradient thing we used for the career simulation in IB and also a proper contrast check and fix for light mode gold color without it being mud colored ... for the powerplay I think the chips should be able to be dragged into the blanks and not just typed. And we can have that same drag interaction we had for match games."

- **Two fonts, one rule (Signal).** Jersey 20 names things: screen titles, the level name in the HUD, term names (bucket names, word chips, match terms), numbers, keys, buttons. Roboto says things: questions, answers, instructions, hints, meta. Nothing under 13px. The old rules had put the profit steps ("Revenue: 500 x $200 =") and the "Revenue rig" label in Jersey at 9px.
- **Profit builder, sort buckets and Power Play in Signal** are now square pixel surfaces with hard shadows, like the options and match tiles (`glossary-signal.css`, the block dated 9 Oct). Power Play lost its rounded, blurred card.
- **Drag ghost:** it renders in a portal on `<body>`, outside the themed shell, so it never saw Signal's styles. It now carries `data-atmosphere` and Signal draws it as a square pixel tile in both modes.
- **Light mode tiles** (options, match tiles, sort items, word chips, profit rows) are white with a 2px edge and a hard 4px shadow; their panels take a pale tint, so tiles lift off the pale city instead of melting into it. Waiting (disabled) buttons are a neutral slab with dark text instead of gold at 40% opacity (grey on pale yellow was under 2:1).
- **Power Play drag:** word chips drag into the blanks with the match game's tether (same line, glow and end dot); the blank under the pointer lights up. A tap fills the blank last focused, else the first empty one. Typing still works. Used chips dim. The tether is an `<svg>` on the screen root so every theme's `div:nth-of-type` rules still hold. Verified with real mouse drags in headless Chrome (sort and Power Play, both modes).
- **Light-mode gold, two tiers.** Fills use the bright `#ffb81f` with dark ink in both themes; text uses a contrast-safe gold. The career Play button is now the IB simulation's gradient (`.career-play-cta` in app.css), and anything on a dark photo declares `on-dark-media`, which puts the dark theme's bright world colours back in light mode (the hero was drawing `#996100` on `#0e0c20`: 3.7:1 and mud). The text rung moved from `#996100` (h38, drifts olive) to `#a85f00` (h34): 4.88:1 on white, 4.64:1 on the `#f7f9ff` frost. Key figures in light are drawn solid in that rung (`--figure-share: 100%`), because the dark theme's white-lifted gradient start washed "Bachelor's degree" out on white.
- **QA shortcut (DEMO-ONLY):** `?q=<n>` opens the level on question n and `?pp=1` on Power Play, so every screen kind can be checked without playing through.
- **Not pushed (local only, as before):** the like removal and the Zack feedback notes. CareerDetailLab and CareerDetailExperience carry both, so only this entry's hunks were staged from them.

## 2026-10-08: Big screens: viewport sizes cancel the page zoom everywhere; glossary questions centred at 4K

**Why:** Chandu, with a 4K screenshot of the glossary game (question and answers stuck at the bottom, a huge empty middle): "please centre the questions and answers and CTAs etc properly across all screen sizes. Also check the student app and counselor dashboard etc and especially the For You page, please make sure things don't go sit on the bottom or the top etc awkwardly."

- Root cause: above 1440px the body zooms (1.1 from 1441x800, 1.25 from 1800x900; globals.css) so every screen looks like the 1440 design scaled up. Zoom multiplies viewport units too, so anything sized in `dvh`/`vh`/`vw` rendered 10 to 25% bigger than the window. The app already had `--vz` for this, but only `.h-dvh`, `.min-h-dvh` and two Explore heights used it. The glossary shell (`height: var(--glossary-visible-height, 100dvh)`) was 125% of the window at 4K, so its centred stage sat below the fold.
- Fix: every viewport length in the app now divides by `--vz` where it is written (`85dvh` becomes `calc(85dvh/var(--vz,1))`), 327 values in 62 files, plus `h-screen`/`min-h-screen`/`max-h-screen`/`h-svh`/`min-h-svh`/`w-screen` in globals.css. Left alone on purpose: image `sizes` hints, media queries, framer-motion animation values (it can't animate calc), the marketing landing and the labs. `--vz` is 1 below 1441px and on Play's no-zoom route, so smaller screens are unchanged.
- Follow-up the same day (Chandu: "fix as much as you can. Do the landing too."): the marketing landing, the labs, the gate page and the unrouted glossary game now divide too (44 more values); negative values (`-50vw` full-bleed margins in Connect, PlayHub's `calc(50%-50vw)`, Build's aurora offsets, two glossary decorations) and lines that mixed fixed and unfixed values (Match card size, GPA picker width) are fixed. The Play trailer's animations can't use calc in framer, so its letterbox bars now sit at their real height and grow in with scaleY, and its colour streak moves in % of its own width. Still raw on purpose: image `sizes` hints and media queries (they already measure the real window), the landing's Dreamy mascot size (its own formula already accounts for --vz), BagSecured's fly-away (runs inside the simulation, where zoom is off) and the motion lab demo. Landing check at 1280x800 to 2560x1400: no sideways scroll, the hero fills the zoomed screen exactly, headline 58 to 72px.
- **New rule:** any new viewport-sized length must divide by `--vz` (`calc(Ndvh/var(--vz,1))`), or it will overflow on big screens.
- Evidence: glossary question gaps above and below are equal at 1280x800 (169/169), 1512x982 (237/237), 1920x1080 (251/251) and 2560x1400 (411/411), shell exactly the window. At 2560x1400, no fixed or sticky element spills past the window edges and nothing scrolls sideways on Home, Play, Connect, Profile, Opportunities, Colleges, a career page, or counselor default, v4 (overview, students, productivity), v5 (overview, students, prepare) and v6. For You fits exactly (no page scroll, the reel card 148 to 1370 of 1400). The career sheet is centred (188 above, 187 below). tsc and lint clean.

## 2026-10-08: One step back, everywhere

**Why:** Chandu: "again, when I hit back to Communities from a board that I opened it should take me to the People tab. ALWAYS EVERYTHING SHOULD GO ONLY ONE STEP BACK. PLEASE FIX THIS APP WIDE. EVERY SINGLE INTERACTION OR SCREEN." Most layers (sheets, dialogs, in-page drill-ins like an industry in People or a program inside a board) were plain React state, so the browser's Back, the iPad swipe and Android Back skipped right past them, and Connect replaced its URL instead of stacking, so Back left Connect entirely.

- **Core, `src/lib/backStep.ts`.** Every layer owns one history entry while open (`dmLayer`). Back onto the entry below closes it; closing it in the app (X, Back, tap outside) takes the entry back off, so no Back press is ever spent on nothing. Our own corrective steps are hidden from Next's router and from other listeners, and any history write made meanwhile waits for them, so "close the sheet and open Play" can't be undone by the cleanup. Every entry is stamped (`dmAt`) so an entry left behind by a layer that is gone (left the page with a sheet open) is skipped in the direction the student was going. Each entry also remembers its scroll, and `ScrollReset` restores it on Back/Forward between pages instead of jumping to the top.
- **Dialogs, `HistoryHost`** (root layout): watches `[role=dialog][aria-modal=true]` and modal `<dialog>`s and gives each one an entry. Back closes it with its own Close button, else Escape. `data-own-history` opts out: the welcome splashes do, since an intro is a gate, not a layer (Back from it goes to the screen before).
- **In-page layers, `useBackStep(open, onClose)`**: People industries and the all-industries list, the United Way program page and profiles, UW e-Mentorship profile, Mentorship program profile and open month, AT&T v1/v2 profiles and Share modes, the pro dashboard's answered list, counselor v4 group detail. Also Opportunities' View all shelf (now back to the spot it was opened from), Profile Settings (back to the tab it was opened from, not always Top 3), Profile's swap and add overlays and the paths compare view, and the step views inside Connect with Professionals and the Play connect interstitial. **Steps, `useBackSteps(depth, onBack)`**: sign-up, the resume builder wizard, PreGame's how-to and lesson, the performance plan, and the Preferences build sections. Confirm dialogs without a Close now take Escape; the ATS check stage opts out (a progress stage, not a layer).
- **Connect**: every move to a new screen is a real history entry with its depth (`dmConnect`); tab switches and a board's own filters replace (they are places, not steps). Back restores the screen it came from and its scroll; after a reload or a return the URL names the screen. Mentorship's program close now steps back instead of pushing the list.
- **Sheets**: leaving the page from inside a career/school sheet (Play, Glossary, a link) remembers the sheet, so one Back lands on the same sheet over the same scroll spot.
- **Route back buttons**: `goBackOr` now only steps back within the app's own entries (`canGoBack`), not out to a previous site. Fixed-destination backs now step back: counselor v5 student page (relabelled "Back", since after Switch student the step back is the previous student) and Prepare, the resume document X, the simulation ending's "Back to Games", and both glossary games. Left alone on purpose: the v4 leader "back to district" (it also switches role).

**Evidence (tablet 768x1024):** Communities > board > Back = Communities at the same scroll; People > profile > browser Back = People at scroll 250; Explore at 700 > sheet > Play > Back = Explore at 700 with the same sheet > Back = sheet closed, no leftover entry; People industry and all-industries > industry each step back one level; UW program > Back = board at 300 > Back = Communities; Explore intro splash closes without leaving an entry. Note: in a hidden browser tab animations stand still, so a closing sheet stays mounted until the tab is visible; HistoryHost waits for visibility before treating a dialog as "didn't close".

## 2026-10-08: United Way, two boards (network and Michigan) on one engine, fleshed out for every role

**Why:** Chandu: "lets please do very detailed research on united way MICHIGAN and rebuild the board for that specifically", then "I dont think the board we had built incorporated any of our broader research either. So build one with the broader network view and one specific to michigan. And it was such a basic board, nothing more than answering questions and seeing some details about a program. Please flesh it out to be super useful for everyone involved."

**Research:** docs/reference/united-way-michigan-research-2026-10-08.md (new; sources for every fact). What it changed: Michigan has about 35 local United Ways and several merged (Lansing, Kalamazoo, Battle Creek and Jackson are one United Way of South Central Michigan; Washtenaw joined Southeastern Michigan; Northwest Michigan closed 30 Sept 2026), so the map shows today's organisations. Detroit's high school career work (College and Career Pathways, "Find Your Future") is 2017 to 2019 history and Grow Detroit's Young Talent is the City's program, so neither is shown as a United Way program (GDYT is named in an Ask answer because Detroit teens need it). No Michigan United Way runs its own high school mentoring; they fund Big Brothers Big Sisters and Winning Futures, so cards say "funded by" and nothing hands off to the Mentorship tab. What they do run for teens is service and leadership (Student United Way, Youth United Way, Youth Genesee Serves, Days of Caring), so the board leads with that.

**Changed:**
- One engine, two data sets: `UnitedWayBoardView` takes `board`; `uwData.NETWORK` (route `united-way-student-success`) and `uwMichigan.MICHIGAN` (route `united-way-michigan`, new Connect community card). The `UwBoard` type in uwData.ts is the contract a third board (another state or one local United Way) fills in.
- Network board now carries the 7 Oct memo's research it had skipped: Palm Beach Mentor Center, Salt Lake Promise Student Advocates, Midlands Young Men United, Miami Career Connections beside Orange County and Southwest Virginia; national partners (BBBS, MENTOR, Character Playbook) on the United Way view. Each network program has its own official photo (three new: uw-net-advocate from Palm Beach, uw-net-college from Orange County, uw-net-intern from unitedway.org).
- Student: Home adds "For you" (program and event matched to Top 3), a "You here" strip of what the student has going on, and 2-1-1 (Michigan: call 211 or text ZIP to 898211). Programs filter by kind, and the sheet adds who it is for, how to join (3 steps), deadline and the program's own page. Events group by month and add to calendar (.ics). New Serve tab: teen volunteer shifts with spots left, a service-hours ring toward 40 and an hours letter (schools, NHS and scholarships ask for hours; Youth United Way is the model). Tabs: Home, Programs, Events, Serve, Ask (Segmented gained `dense` so five fit at 375).
- Volunteer: Today opens with "Since you were last here", questions routed to the volunteer answered inline (contact info blocked), quick requests and the next shift. New Shifts tab with length filter and sign-up. My Impact adds team standings for the workplace campaign and notes from students.
- United Way: Impact adds a 30-day trend, careers students saved and what they ask about (what to program next), plus context (Michigan: 67% of households led by someone under 25 are below ALICE, 2026 update). Programs gets a Post tool that publishes an event or shift straight to the student and volunteer views. New Volunteers tab: check status per volunteer with reminders, hours by company.
- Map: pins sit at real longitude and latitude (Albers fit to @svg-maps/usa), with a Michigan frame for the Michigan board.

**Demo-only:** per-United-Way counts, activity numbers, several dates (flagged DEMO-ONLY in uwMichigan.ts), Youth United Way's status (not confirmed current).

**Evidence:** tsc and eslint clean on the touched files. Both boards checked in the preview at 1360 and 375: all four views, Serve sign-up, partner Impact layout, both maps.

**Next:** confirm with United Way which Michigan programs are live this year and whether a Michigan pilot would sit with one local United Way or the state association (uwmich.org). Push only when Chandu says push.

## 2026-10-06 — Signal, the full pass: one bar, one type system, every component, drag to the buckets, the dialogue-box feedback, the Levels map

**Why:** Chandu, over a run of the Signal glossary with screenshots: the feedback card ("the why is too small and nobody is gonna click that. Show the feedback in the box without needing the tap ... add the Nintendo style typing-in effect, the tap to show at once thing and the continue CTA ... a bit of parallax on the background"); the HUD ("the whole HUD with the progress bar can be merged with the top nav ... they are HUGE, shrink them down considerably, do they have to be rows?"); the match question ("still carries Drift's styling ... I can't see the artwork, have the images BIGGER and visible, the words can come under, tiles on both columns the same width and height"); fonts ("keep fonts consistent, every screen is having different fonts"); the buckets ("wasn't intuitive, I should be able to drag to the buckets and everything should give feedback, and I had to scroll"); the finish screen (dim text: "so many glaring issues, go through every component and update to the pixel art style"); the Levels map ("horribly broken, nothing lines up, nothing makes sense and it doesn't tell the user anything"); and "Dreamy can be larger, graphics need to pop more".

**What:**
- **Feedback as a dialogue box** (`FeedbackPanel`, `useTypewriter`): the verdict is a name tab over the box ("Correct!" in gold, "Not quite" in pink), the explanation is in the box from the start and types in at 60 characters a second with a caret while the cloud's mouth moves (`talking` on `DreamyFace`/`SignalCloud`); tapping the box, Enter or Space finishes the line at once, then a second tap goes on; a bobbing chevron marks "done" and the Continue button fades in. Reduced motion shows the line whole. Every theme gets the inline explanation and the typing; Signal gets the box, border and hard shadow.
- **The skyline drifts** slowly left and right over 110 seconds, a side-scroller's parallax, off under reduced motion.
- **A slim stacked HUD.** A one-row try (the HUD inside the top bar, `TopBar` still has the `hud` slot) was pulled back on Chandu's call ("the milestone circles can be under the progress bar ... if the stacked version was better do that, but make the top nav shorter"): the nav row is 48px, and under it one strip on the same panel carries the lesson and its count, the bar, and the five 30px term circles under the bar with the mastered count at their right. No labels under the circles (each names its term on hover and to a screen reader). The stage below is centred in the free height on every screen.
- **One type system:** the pixel face (Press Start 2P) for titles, labels, keys, buttons, the question and short answers (multiple-choice answers, match tiles, sort tokens); the mono for sentences (definitions, explanations, descriptions). One surface language: panels `--sig-panel` with a 1px `--sig-line` edge and a hard offset shadow, tiles `--sig-card` with a #2e3650 edge, square corners, cyan selected, green right, pink wrong. Applied to match, sort, type, document, profit, Power Play, the finish and the map.
- **Match:** the picture sits above the word in every tile, tiles in both columns share one width and one height (`grid-auto-rows: 1fr`), heights clamped to viewport so five rows fit the fold; the pairing dot rides the corner.
- **Sort buckets:** tokens can be dragged onto a bucket (HTML5 drag on mouse and trackpad; tap-then-tap stays, and is the only way on touch); the bucket lights while a token is over it and pops when it lands, each shows its count, placed tokens pop in; the hint line changes with the state. Two bucket columns hold down to 480px; nothing scrolls.
- **Finish screen:** pixel title in gold, the score panel, mono rows, the burst under the words (text was reading dim).
- **Answer tiles' pictures are all or nothing** per question (`OptionList`), so four tiles always share one shape.
- **Levels map, every theme:** a legend under the title ("17 levels. Each one teaches five words. Finish a level to unlock the next one and a bigger deal."), a tier heading where each tier starts, and each level as one aligned row: number or lock, title, what the level is for (`goal`), its five words, minutes, "Unlocks a $X deal", and Playing now / Locked. Signal draws it as a ledger.
- **Bigger cloud** beside the question (up to 176px); answer art 56px and the Misuse Review's row pictures 64px, contained, on 72px rows (Chandu: "the image and their scale is wrong in the Misuse Review question, I cannot see the images properly").

**Validation:** tsc, eslint; Signal run in the preview at 648px, 800px and 1024px: question, match (pairs solved), sort (tokens placed), the feedback box typing and finishing, the one-row bar, the map. Not reached in the preview this pass: the finish screen (the question loop repeats missed terms), so its restyle is from the CSS, not a screenshot.

**Why:** Chandu: "the graphic posts that professionals have on the feed, they should be visible on their profiles where we see their posts and the community boards ... **What:**

- **Boards** (`AlignedInsightRow`): a graphic post is the graphic full width with caption and one row of actions (Helpful, replies, Save, time) under it; no avatar column, head line or right-hand count column.
- **Profiles and the pro dashboard:** Posts lists show the graphic and its caption instead of the title; seed graphic posts were title-only there before.
- **Composer:** no title and no caption step for a graphic post. One always-visible caption field sits under the preview ("Add a caption (optional)"), Share is live as soon as there are words on the picture, and the post's headline (where a screen needs one) is the graphic's own words.

- **Second pass** (Chandu, with screenshots: "the posts got too big to be full width ... caption too close to the stats"; then on a card-sized attempt, "don't cap it at card size like this. It needs to be aligned better and read like a post still. It needs some sort of label too"; "this scale also messes up the designation and company lockup"; "see how Twitter, Instagram, Reddit on desktop handle these things"). What each does on desktop: X keeps media in the text column, never under the avatar, with a height cap near 510px (and crops tall images, which would cut our credit line); Instagram stacks media full width, then actions, then a clamped caption; Reddit centres a portrait image at a capped height and fills the room either side with a blurred copy of the image. Taken together: a graphic post keeps the 44px gutter with a post-type glyph where the avatar sits, so its column lines up with every other post; a label row ("Post from a Dream Volunteer · Business & Finance · 5d ago") with Follow and the menu where other posts have them; the graphic in a full-column frame 500px tall, centred, with a blurred dimmed copy of its own background filling the sides (`FramedGraphic`; no frame under 640px); the caption under it as a clamped excerpt with Read more (the body with the graphic's own words taken off the front, `captionFor`, so the line is never read twice); counts last with more room. Boards show the graphic always (it was behind the feed-v2 flag), stacked like the Feed (Chandu: "on smaller devices the post and captions should not be side by side. Do they even need to be side by side on desktop? I doubt this is how the competitors do it"; none of the three do): a quiet head line, the framed picture at 480px, the caption, one action row, inside the board's glass row. The Feed's frame is 580px tall (picture 464px wide) after "now the images are TOO SMALL". The credit on the graphic is measured entirely in container units now, the avatar (9cqi) and the company mark (`CompanyMark unit="em"`) included, and the role line never wraps, so the lockup holds at 200px and 560px.

- **Third pass: one visual language** (Chandu: "make it consistent with the rest of the board. The replies, views etc should match the other posts. There should be ONE VISUAL LANGUAGE for these tabs, columns and posts, and terminology ... make sure the text is legible, I think we're shrinking text too much on smaller devices ... revert to the post having the pfp and username designation ... let's have the other tabs, questions, posts etc look like the feed UI too"; and "in a person's profile they don't need the pfp and name and designation"). Every post wears the Feed's author row again, graphic posts included (the framed picture, caption and counts follow it). A board's Questions and Posts tabs are now the Feed's own rows (`FeedPostRow`) in the Feed's hairline-divided panel, so comments, likes, views, Save and Share read the same everywhere and "replies" and "Helpful" are gone from boards; every question is the student's row (Chandu: "questions should be from students in the questions tab, answers can show up in that feed but let's keep questions and posts separate and have that student element, with their avatars"): their avatar, handle, grade and time, the question, then the pro's answer as a quoted reply beneath with a straight 2px rule down its left, square ends, and their small portrait and name (the first cut's rule carried a border radius so it curved at both ends, which Chandu read as "a bug or a mistake"; a surface instead of a rule was rejected too: "just design them better"), or the status chip while it waits (`BoardThreadRow`); every list of posts outside the Feed (board Questions and Posts, the profile's Answers & Posts) is locked to the Feed's column, 696px at xl and the full column below (`FEED_COL` in primitives), so one width rules desktop, tablet and phone alike; breathers keep their slots between panel segments (`BoardFeedList`). ## 2026-10-06 — Leaderboard: leagues of thirty, and the quieter page

**Why:** Joshua's final direction on the leaderboard (Slack, 6 Oct): "We're simplifying this into 4 semester-leagues based on relative rank: Bronze, Silver, Gold, Diamond. About 120 participating students, so roughly 30 students per league ... Standings update daily ... The goal is for every student to have something visible to compete for, rather than only showing a Top 25. Eventually a student should clearly see something like: Silver League • #6 of 30 • 180 points to Gold." On the UI: "Keep New York vs New Jersey | ASE | Central as 3 equal-width, symmetrical tabs across the top ... make the rivalry the main section underneath. Simplify the rivalry significantly ... identify each side once, show the score, and only keep the donut/circle if it genuinely helps. Put My Rank underneath the rivalry, not beside it. Then show the leaderboard below My Rank. Remove the progress bars beside student points. Reduce metadata in each row ... Use NJ and NY instead of school name. Keep the student's own row highlighted and give the Top 3 slightly stronger recognition." His Replit (dceeai.replit.app/leaderboard/regional) is the structure; ours is "cleaner, simpler, and less dense".

**What:**
- **Data** (`src/components/leaderboard/data.ts`): `LEAGUES`, `LEAGUE_SIZE = 30` and `leagueFor(rank)` (ranks 1 to 30 Diamond, 31 to 60 Gold, 61 to 90 Silver, 91 to 120 Bronze). The Replit's 25 students stay as ranks 1 to 25; 95 seeded students fill ranks 26 to 120 so every league has its thirty (ASE is New York, Central is New Jersey; the 80 portraits are used first and the rest draw initials, `avatar` is now optional). Noah Williams is still "you": #8 overall, so Diamond.
- **Page** (`LeaderboardExperience.tsx`, rewritten; DEMO-ONLY), top to bottom in Joshua's order: (1) three equal tabs; (2) who is winning: on NY vs NJ one card with each state's crest, name and count of students in Diamond today, LEADS under the leader, one split bar, no donut (it added nothing a bar does not); on a school tab that school's count per league; (3) My Rank as one full-width card: "Diamond League • #8 of 30 • 2,115 points clear of Gold" (the top league shows its cushion over the first place of Gold; every other league shows the points to the league above, so the line always names something to play for), with name, state and total points in a single sub-line; (4) the league's thirty, with league chips defaulting to the student's own league. A row is place, portrait or initials, name, NY/NJ chip, points: no bars, no school, no grade. The league's top three wear a medal with a crown on first; your row is the only tinted one. A footnote states the league bands and that standings update daily. The old stadium design (lights, jumbo scoreboard, team cards, XP bars) is gone.

- **Marks.** Chandu asked whether NY and NJ "have any kind of flag system we should use": both state flags are the arms on a field, New York's dark blue and New Jersey's buff, and the arms are far too detailed for 40px, so the field colours are the system: NY blue, NJ buff, on the shields, the split bar, the LEADS tag and every row's NY/NJ chip. A pennant version was tried and rejected ("the flag vectors are bad, try something else. Shields are fine. But better designed somehow"); the shields are now a heater shape with a lit top, a fine inner line and the letters on the optical centre. The schools' own marks (asehs.org's eagle diamond, Central's blue devil from nps.k12.nj.us/CTL) sit on the school card as a ringed 56px plate, which is the one place they read as identity rather than clutter (`public/images/schools/`).

## 2026-10-06 — World UI: premium pass and the scalable instrument library

**Why:** Chandu, on the world-UI batch: "the report forms, the spreadsheets etc. All of them need better designs, alignments, spacing, layout etc. so please do a full premium upgrade of what's been built first", and before that: "dialogue box skin transitions etc. Are these all scalable? ... eventually 900 careers." The first round was written for three careers: "Riverbend · Four West", "Cobalt Capital", "Kestrel Aero Maintenance" and a MAR sheet were literal strings in `WorldUi.tsx`, each sheet had its own paper and header, and a fourth career would have meant a fourth copy. "Then do what you suggest to make it everything scalable, then only commit and push."

**What (one commit, with round two):**
- **Two primitives carry every instrument.** `Paper` (a document: header line, title left and meta right, a rule in the world colour, then rows on one 40 px grid) and `Device` (equipment: dark glass, one inner stroke, tracked-caps header). The record sheet, report sheet and logbook are all `Paper`; the monitor, clock, lights board and elevator are all `Device`. One `Chip` for every status. That is the premium pass: the same type sizes, rules, radii and spacing on every sheet, instead of three hand-tuned ones.
- **Skin by world.** `worldSkin(world)` maps the app's worlds to a paper stock, a device palette and a glow (health worlds: clinical white and green; trades: cream stock and amber; tech: cool white and cyan; default: warm stock and amber). The clock's digits, the elevator's indicator and the paper under a chart all take it, so a new career in an existing world needs no colour work.
- **Names from context.** `WorldContext` (`{ firm, place, world }`) is provided once by `SimulationPlayer` from `simulation.firm`, the new `Level.place` ("Four West") and `simulation.world`. No instrument names a firm any more; `badge.org`, `inbox.org`, `elevator.label` and `monitor.place` are optional overrides. The rapid inbox's sender line reads `beat.speaker` and the new `beat.speakerRole` instead of a hard-coded "Christina · Associate".
- **Generic kinds.** `callBoard` is `lights` (any rows naming Room / Bed / Bay / Gate / Line / Table / Stand / Dock), `mar` is `record` with its rows in data, `report` is `sheet` with `title`, `meta`, `lines`. The RN and IB level files carry the rows and labels now.
- **Outcome contract.** Every instrument that can react takes `outcome` (the locked answer's tier) and decides its own reaction; the table is in the spec.
- **Spec:** `docs/handoff/specs/world-ui.md` (kinds, fields, outcome table, how a career adopts it in four steps). Listed in `docs/HANDOFF_INDEX.md`.

**Validation:** tsc, eslint and `next build --webpack` clean. Every instrument re-checked in the preview on the live v2 levels: RN badge, wristband, stable and alarm monitors (header now "Riverbend · Four West" from context), lights board, record sheet, night report; IB inbox ("Inbox · Cobalt Capital", "Christina · Associate" from data), elevator ("Cobalt Capital" from context), 3 PM clock with Deck cell, 6 PM Delivered. ## 2026-10-05 — Hands-on torque wrench (built as a local experiment, now in the AMT v2 LAB)

**Why:** Chandu: "can we do an interactive animated torque wrench usage with the clicking etc? ... This one can be a local experiment."

**What:**
- **`TorqueBeat` and `TorqueBody.tsx`:** an illustrated click-type torque wrench on a leaking fluid-line fitting.
  - **Set:** drag the setting into the manual's green mark (shown on the wrench's scale and the slider track). Releasing outside it shakes and doesn't lock.
  - **Tighten:** hold to pull. The handle swings, the fitting turns, ratchet ticks play and tension builds to the setting.
  - **The click:** at the setting the head breaks with a CLICK. There's a new `playTorqueClick` sound, the handle flicks and the bar turns green.
  - **Release on time:** letting go within 650ms is "Strong move!". Holding past it over-tightens: the bar turns red and the verdict reads "Not quite.", explaining the fitting can crack.
  - **Re-gripping:** a pull released before the click keeps its tension, like re-gripping a ratchet.
  - **Timing:** the pull runs on a 30ms real-clock timer, not animation frames, so the click lands at the same moment on a throttled Chromebook.
- **AMT-18b:** this beat replaces the step-ordering list, so no screen is added. It shows its own verdict, so a miss is explained.
- **Validated:** both paths were checked in the preview.

**Shipped:** in the AMT v2 LAB (see the entry above).

## 2026-10-05 — Hair-safe cutouts in `art:extract`

**Why:** Chandu: "make sure the cutouts do hair well, I don't want backgrounds slipping in through curls etc."

**What:**
- The Swift helper now writes full-frame Vision masks, and `scripts/play-art/lib/refine.mjs` does the cut.
- Within a band around the outline, alpha is re-solved by projecting each pixel onto the local hair to background colour line. The hair colour is sampled near the outline, falling back to a wider sample for thin outer curls; the background comes from the real scene just outside the person.
- **Goes clear:**
  - pixels matching the background (24px or 8px estimates);
  - enclosed pockets that are bright and match a 56px background estimate;
  - Vision's glow more than a band outside the outline;
  - small specks, judged by their solid core.
- **Edges:** colour un-mixing is clamped between the pixel's own colour and the hair colour; it was overshooting into pale blobs.
- **Kept:** painted rim light and jewellery.
- **Verified:** on dark and magenta backgrounds at 2x, and in a phone-scale composite over the hangar plate. The before and after is at `art-intake/aviation-maintenance-technician/cutouts/_hair-before-after.jpg`.

## 2026-10-05 — No-Codex art path: `art:extract` and SOP chapter 9 (first run: AMT)

**Why:** Chandu, starting Aviation Maintenance Technician: "We don't have the sprites and separate backgrounds etc for this like we had for the others... I'm also out of codex credits... We need an SOP to do this and hopefully automate this whole process for newer games that are coming too."

**What:**
- **`npm run art:extract -- <career>`** (`scripts/play-art/lib/extract.mjs`, plus a Swift Vision helper in `scripts/play-art/native/`, compiled on first run into a gitignored `.bin/`):
  - It reads `art-intake/<career>/scenes/`.
  - A scene with no detected person goes to `plates/`.
  - Each separable person becomes a transparent cutout in `cutouts/`, via Vision's foreground instance mask, kept only if it contains a person from `VNDetectHumanRectanglesRequest`.
  - A cutout that holds two or more people sends its scene to `heroes/`.
  - It also writes `_sheet.jpg` and `assign.json`.
- **`--assign`:** copies the named cutouts into `sprites/`, and switches the manifest to waist-up when the cutouts stop at the scene's bottom edge.
- **`slotFor(manifest)`:** auto-placement now stands a waist-up career's characters on `WAIST_UP_SLOT` `{ x: .5, baselineY: .99, heightFrac: .9 }`, which is what IB uses.
- **SOP chapter 9:** steps, the automatic-versus-manual split, limits, and paste-ready prompts. It is linked from the SOP index and chapter 8.

**First run (AMT), on 7 supplied images:**
- **Plates:** hangar-wide, landing-gear, workshop.
- **Heroes:** gear-leak-pov, toolbox-pov.
- **Cutouts:** Maya ×2, one unnamed technician, one male technician.
- **Assigned:** maya-welcoming and maya-proud. **Still needed:** maya-concerned (prompt 4.1 in chapter 9).

**Not started:** the AMT level itself (40 screens, new interactions: find the missing tool, tap-to-inspect, measured vs limit, build the response).

### 2026-10-02 Dreamy 3D: the real model running live in the browser (`/dreamy-lab/3d`)

- WHY (user): "I definitely need to wire these into the app so it can react
  dynamically as opposed to just playing a video, and it can float around
  and have different angles... IS that possible without slowing down the
  app?" This page is the feasibility answer, behind the hamburger's lab
  links ("Dreamy 3D"), DEMO-ONLY, nothing in the demo imports it.
- WHAT: three.js (new dependency, `three` + `@types/three`) loaded only on
  this route via next/dynamic ssr:false. `src/components/dreamy-lab/live/`:
  - `dreamyRig.ts` maps the Blender rig onto the glTF: every control is a
    CTRL_EMOTION slider, and morph weights use the same driver
    expressions as Blender (mouth Smile/Oh/Closed/Concern, lid rim
    Blink/Joy/Concern/Wonder, body stub/wave). Blender carves the eyes and
    mouth with live booleans, which glTF cannot carry, so the body ships
    WITHOUT holes and the fragment shader discards an ellipse per eye and
    a D for the mouth, sized per expression from the measured Blender
    cutters. The compressor quantizes positions and moves the scale into
    the node, so the cut-outs run through the body node's matrix (uNode).
  - `brain.ts` is the state machine: idle float, random blinks (close
    70 ms, hold 40, open 120, right lid a frame late), gaze darts, follow
    the pointer, and nine one-shot reactions with their props. Every
    control rides a damped spring so interruptions never pop.
  - `DreamyLiveCanvas.tsx`: DPR capped at 1.75 (1 in low-power), 30 fps cap
    in low-power, rendering pauses when off screen or the tab is hidden,
    drag to turn (drifts back), tap for happy. `?nopause=1` keeps it
    rendering in hidden tabs, for automated checks only.
- MODEL: `public/models/dreamy/dreamy.opt.glb` (~0.5 MB, meshopt) plus
  baked iris textures. Rebuild with `scripts/dreamy-export-web.sh`
  (Blender background export + gltf-transform). Gotchas: keep
  `--join false` (it merged props) and `--prune-attributes false` (it
  dropped the iris UVs); props over 6k triangles are decimated (the heart
  was 186k from bevel + subsurf).
- COST measured on the dev Mac: 1 to 6 ms of work per frame. Not yet
  measured on a Chromebook; that is the real test.
- KNOWN GAP (user, same day): "it's lost a lot of its lighting and shading
  and depth". Expected: Blender renders with Cycles path tracing
  (subsurface, soft translucency); the browser gets a fast physical
  material and an environment map. Closing that gap means baked lighting
  textures or a custom shader. The user asked to try real Blender
  renders for the welcome modals next instead (local only).

### 2026-10-02 Blender: motion add-ons on the new Dreamy model (wave + soft float)

- WHAT: the user replaced our model with a new one built elsewhere
  (`~/Documents/Dreamari/outputs/dreamy-refinement/dreamy-performance.blend`)
  and asked to stop all look work: "the model is working perfectly we just
  need to understand how to add the wave animation without it looking bad
  and maybe a little more dynamic soft floaty movements to the body so it
  doesn't move rigid". Also: "dont wire any eyes or anything".
- WHERE: a copy, `dreamy-performance-anim.blend` in the same folder. The
  original file is untouched. Everything added lives in collection
  `03 ADD-ON • soft float + wave` plus three new modifiers; turning the
  modifiers off returns the exact original behaviour.
- HOW, and why this way:
  - Soft float = `LATTICE • soft float` (3x3x3, parented to the BODY
    bone) added as the LAST modifier on the body AND on all 14 face
    meshes, so eyes/mouth deform identically and never slide off the
    body. Five lattice shape keys (breathe, sway, bob, side_puff, tilt)
    run on slow Noise F-modifiers (action "Dreamy • soft float (always
    on)"), so it layers over any animation without editing it. A Soft
    Body on the lattice (goal 1.0 bottom layer, 0.62 top) adds
    follow-through: on a hop the top lags, overshoots and settles.
  - Wave = `LATTICE • wave puff` (7x5x9, around the right side puff,
    before Soft float in the body stack). The puff itself swells up-and-
    out into a rounded stub; no separate hand object, because a stuck-on
    sphere leaves a hard seam. Two new sliders on CTRL_EMOTION, `stub`
    (0..1.5) and `wave` (-1..1, only acts once the stub is out). A
    3-point and a 5-point cage were tried first: the first barely moved,
    the second stretched the side into a pointed fin. A flat-topped
    falloff on the dense cage keeps the tip round.
  - New action "Dreamy • hello wave" (52 frames at 18 fps): anticipation
    squash, pop out with overshoot, three waves with a body bob, happy
    blink, tuck in with a small rebound, settle. Only existing controls
    plus the two new sliders are keyed.
- REVISION (same day): the whole-body float was REMOVED (user: "its
  moving like water now, dont do that. Revert to rigid and just have some
  of the puffy parts be a tiny bit wobbly"). Replaced by three small
  per-puff lattices (top, left, right): boundary pinned, only the inside
  of each puff jiggles about 2 cm on slow noise and lags a little on
  hops via soft body. The wave cage was rebuilt as a dense 7x5x9 cage
  with a flat-topped falloff and a pivot at the puff base so the tip
  stays round. Upswings limited, since a full upswing bent it into a fin.
- BUG I caused and fixed: setting test poses from Python with whole
  numbers (`ctrl["mouth_open"]=0`) silently turned ten CTRL_EMOTION
  sliders into INTEGER properties, so animation rounded 0.8 to 0 and
  every mouth snapped shut. All are floats again. Always assign
  `float(...)` to custom properties.
- TIMELINE: the file only ever played the 72-frame "delight" clip, which
  is why the user saw nothing else. All clips now sit on one NLA track
  with markers: delight 1-72, wave 80-131, expression library 140-391
  (happy, curious, nervous, alert, idea, love, party, 36 frames each,
  rebuilt from the 2D PNGs in public/images/dreamy/v2), old pose sheet
  400-680 (a copy with more open mouths; the original is kept).
- LIMITS: closed eyes are flat lines, not the upward happy arcs in the
  2D love/party art, because the rig's blink is the only closed shape and

  mark, sweat drop) are not modeled.
- FORM LOCK (user: "the body moves too much and loses its form after the
  wink... it should always keep its form and anatomy"): the three per-puff
  wobble lattices were removed too. Their soft-body simulation drifted
  over the timeline. Measured afterwards in the BODY bone's own space,
  the body's size is identical on every frame except the wave stub.
- PROPS (collection `04 PROPS`, parented to the BODY bone): question mark,
  sweat drop, two exclamations, light bulb, heart, confetti, glasses.
  Each scales in from zero with a small overshoot via CTRL_EMOTION
  sliders prop_question / prop_drop / prop_alert / prop_bulb /
  prop_heart / prop_confetti / prop_glasses, keyed inside the expression
  library. An eighth "smart" expression was added for the glasses, and
  the old pose sheet moved to frame 440. Two gotchas: anything parented
  to BODY inherits its rotated axes, so props are placed by world matrix

- WHAT: `blender/dreamy/dreamy.blend` (untracked, Blender 5.2.2 LTS, EEVEE
  only) is the first 3D Dreamy. Renders for every iteration are in

- WHY (the user's brief, quoted): "a fully rigged dreamy character with

  need to for whichever emote"; puff motion "subtle, lightweight, like really
  light puffs of clouds just bobbing".
- HOW (decisions that could be second-guessed):
  - Body = 11 overlapping spheres, each a drifting empty (`Lobe_N`), realized
    as one mesh in Geometry Nodes, then Mesh to Volume on a Volume object with
    Volume Displace wisps and a Principled Volume shader whose density is
    eroded by animated 4D noise (edges dissipate and re-form). A metaball
    blend and a solid SSS mesh were both built and rejected: metaball read
    as one lump, the mesh read as clay.
  - A GN-generated volume (Points to Volume) silently renders with EEVEE's
    default material and ignores all shader edits; Set Material on it renders
    nothing. That cost most of the afternoon. The mesh-then-modifier route is
    the only one that honors the material.
  - Eyes are flat navy night-sky ovals (star flecks, lighter rim sweep, big
    catchlight + 4-point sparkle, thin clear dome for wet reflection). Iris,
    pupil and refractive-cornea layers were built per the Disney-eye
    tutorials and removed: on this character they read as a bullseye and
    "scary". Eye outline changes come from the `EyeClip` shader group
    (invisible lid boundary: height, slant, curve, per-eye narrowing), not
    from lid meshes.
  - Mouth = D-shaped navy cavity with depth gradient and a flat glossy tongue;
    reshaped per emotion by scale drivers + a "Wavy" shape key (nervous).
  - Physics = `PuffPhysics` soft-body proxy (one vertex per puff, goal to
    the BODY bone, gravity zeroed); lobe empties are vertex-parented so puffs
    lag and settle when the body moves. Noise f-curves add the idle bob.
  - Rig `Dreamy_Rig`: ROOT/BODY/FACE/EYE_L/R (damped-track to LOOK)/MOUTH/
    ARM_L/R/CTRL_FACE. CTRL_FACE props joy, surprised, curious, nervous,
    blink, mouth_open, hands drive every expression; `hands` morphs two stub
    puffs out of the arm bones (0 = absent).
- LATE-SESSION PIVOT (user: "it can still look like a 3d pixar character,

  wrong, ray-cast the evaluated mesh before guessing at shader values.

  changed in the 300-frame demo, and the rule behind each:
  - Blink = close in 3 frames, hold, open in 5 with a 1-frame lid
    overshoot; right lid runs 1 frame behind the left (new `blink_r`
    prop). "Eyes close slowly and then open fast" in his reference, but
    his keys put the close fast and the open slower with a settle; lids
    never move identically.
  - Gaze changes happen under the lids: LOOK is keyed to arrive while
    `blink` is at 1 ("watch the black to see when it turns").
  - Holds are real holds: LOOK keys are copied forward, then one 2-frame
    micro-dart per hold; no easing-sail across holds.
  - Eyes lead the body: LOOK moves 3 frames before the mouth opens on
    surprised; pupils/eye size widen 3 frames after the lids open (new
    `dilate` prop, keyed late).
  - One long "thinking" blink (hold 7) and one quick blink (hold 1).
  - The wave's gaze follows the waving hand side a little.
  Ranges live in `src/components/dreamy-lab/sequence.ts`.
- 2026-10-02 REFERENCE-MATCH PASS (user: "nowhere near what the mascot
  actually looks like... get some references and tutorials and see how
  this is done by experts"). Worked side by side against
  `public/images/dreamy/v2/dreamy-happy.png` (composites in the session
  scratchpad, `ref_pass1..8.png` in renders/). What fixed it, and the
  source for each:
  - View Transform Standard, not AgX (AgX mutes the flat pastel colors):
    strayspark.studio toon guide.
  - 3-point AREA lights with the RenderGuide ratios (fill about half the
    key, rim about half the fill), warm key, cool fill so shadows shift
    blue instead of gray: renderguide.com lighting tutorial, strayspark
    ("hue-shift shadows toward blue").
  - Body = Principled with subsurface 0.5 / radius (1,1.2,1.6) / scale 0.4,
    roughness 0.36, coat 0.6, base tint ramp #9DC0EC -> #DDEBFA by height.
    The emission/Shader-to-RGB toon shell was dropped: it blows out to
    flat white on a light background. Soft-SSS-for-cartoon is the Blender
    Studio "Wing It!" and Wikibooks SSS guidance.
  - World = light-blue-to-white sky gradient at 0.35 so the coat and the
    eye dome have something to reflect (Blender Artists eye threads: glossy
    eyes need an environment to reflect).
  - Eyes = flat navy night-sky ovals (#061030 -> #0E2466 -> #2C56C4 sweep)
    with dark outline disc, big white oval catchlight, 4-point star mesh,
    clear dome with a dim fresnel gloss. The iris-ring + pupil layers
    (built after the Pixar-eye tutorials) were removed again: the art has no
    visible iris, and the ring read as a bullseye. Eyes sit proud of the
    body (y -0.98) because the convex shell was slicing their outer edges.
  - Absolute light levels matter more than ratios: key 800 W blew the SSS
    body to white; 380 W key / 170 fill / 90 rim is the working set.
- REFERENCES reviewed (transcripts pulled by a research agent): the four
  cloud videos and the Caesar/Danny Mac eye series. Takeaways applied:
  Standard view transform, sun key, Volume tile size 2; techniques noted for
  later: empty-driven spherical-gradient fake light for puff shading, the
  emissive highlight object visible only via cornea reflection.
- NEXT: beauty render at 100% and a short animation; a fake-light pass so
  the puffs shade like the reference art; glTF/2.5D export path for the app.

### 2026-10-02 Welcome first, then the page (app-wide rule); every welcome's blur was being stripped by the build; faces placed in the Top 3 band

- **Why.** Chandu: "the profile welcome modal still loads after the page loads. We need to open on the modal everywhere. First the modal with the blurred background, then the page loads. Rule of thumb."
- **Cause.** Every welcome decided whether to show after hydration (storage is client-only), and some waited on top of that (Profile 900ms, Resume 700ms). So the server-rendered page always painted first.
- **Fix** (`src/components/app/SplashVeil.tsx`). (1) An inline script in the root layout's head runs before first paint: if this route's welcome is due (same session rule as `demoSeenThisSession`; reload clears it; `/profile?welcome=1` forces it; `/match-grid` always), it sets `html[data-splash="pending"]`, and globals.css lays the welcome's blurred scrim over the page from the first frame. (2) Every welcome opens in a layout effect with no delay (FirstVisitSplash, Connect's PeopleWelcome, Resume, Profile). (3) The veil lifts only when a welcome opens or a page reports none is due (`liftSplashVeil`); Play mounts its welcome late, and a fixed two-frame lift flashed the page first. The script keeps a 4s safety lift; client-side navigation clears it.
- **The blur bug, app-wide.** The welcome scrim's `backdrop-filter` computed to "none" on every page: with the `-webkit-backdrop-filter` + `backdrop-filter` pair, the build drops BOTH declarations (measured; the unprefixed line alone survives). Fixed in WelcomeSplash.module.css and the build-flow footer in globals.css; those were the only two pairs in .css files (inline style objects are unaffected). The build also flattened `color-mix()` with a `var()` fallback to an opaque colour in the veil, so the veil uses plain rgba. Welcomes also render through a portal at the body (wrapped in `.marketing-v2 themeable` for tokens), since a card with its own backdrop blur becomes the blur's root and the page behind showed sharp.
- **Explore's welcome is back.** The live /explore is ExploreLab, which dropped the welcome while it was an internal lab copy ("no splash in the lab") and never got it back when it went live.
- **Top 3 how-to banner.** Chandu: "stays in that state too long, cut that time in half and let it transition to the Explore state; remove one of the shimmers." Hold 3s to 1.5s; the word sweep is gone, the faster beam and one pulse remain.
- **Faces in the Top 3 band.** Chandu: "when the image headers are made shorter, place the face and a little context of the subject in clear view." No face model is installed (and one would mean a download), so faces were placed by eye on gridded contact sheets of all 162 career photos, converted per photo (its aspect, a ~340px card, the 112px band) so the face lands about 40% down the band, then every band was rendered and reviewed and twelve corrected. Map in `src/components/profile/headerFocus.ts`; a photo without an entry falls back to `photoFocus`.
- **My Build nudge gone missing.** Chandu: "I don't see the nudge or coachmark for My Build anymore." Not broken: one click on My Build retired it in localStorage for good. In demo mode the opened flag now follows the welcomes' rule (`demoSeenThisSession`), so it comes back on every new session or reload; with demo mode off it stays once-ever. Measured: an old localStorage flag no longer hides it; opening My Build retires it for the session.
- **Top 3 how-to banner timing, settled.** Chandu: 3s "was too long", 1.5s "is short; people will scroll a bit if it isn't fast enough and not see the nudge change to the Explore one." Hold is 2.5s (about one read of the 11-word line). The real problem was the clock: it ran only at full visibility and restarted from zero whenever the banner left view, so a small scroll reset it. It now counts while 60% of the banner is visible and pauses and resumes instead of restarting.
- **Career bookmarks hover-only, saved or not.** Chandu: "remove the saved icons from the Explore page too, only show on hover", then "only for careers, keep it for schools." The poster rule no longer exempts saved careers; school cards keep their visible bookmark (a brief school-card change was reverted). Touch screens keep poster bookmarks visible. Measured: 0 of 72 posters (8 saved) show a bookmark at rest.
- **Explore row peek waits for the welcome.** Chandu: "the Explore side scroll nudge should play after the welcome modal is dismissed; it plays too soon while the modal is up." `SplashVeil.tsx` now exposes `useWelcomeInFront()` (true while any welcome is open or the pre-paint veil is on; true during server render); WelcomeSplash registers itself while open. The first Browse row adds `dm-row-peek` only once nothing is in front, so its 1.2s lead-in starts at dismissal; the For You swipe hint waits the same way. Measured: no peek class during the welcome, added on dismiss.
- **My Build nudge, properly this time.** Chandu, again: "I still don't see the My Build nudge and coachmark." Two real causes. (1) The nudge only exists in v2 (My Build is a header icon there; in v1 it is a tab), and a plain visit, such as the nav's Profile link, opened v1 because the v2 choice didn't stick. DEMO-ONLY now: the layout chosen this session (chip, `?v=2`, any Save/Top 3 CTA) sticks in sessionStorage (`dreamari:profile-layout`). (2) The demo "opened" flag was meant to clear on reload like the welcomes, but `clearOnReload` only clears keys under `dreamari:welcome:`; the flag is now `dreamari:welcome:build-opened`. Measured: tag shows, opening My Build retires it, a reload brings it back, and /profile from the nav opens v2 with the tag.
- **My Build rows.** Joshua: "separate Skills and Software to be their own tabs so it is not so long; put Work Style at the bottom." `PreferencesTab.tsx`: Skills (have, want to build) and Software (know, want to learn) are separate rows with their own editors; order is Industries, Saved Careers, Subjects, Education, College & Trade School, Skills, Software, Internship & Job Preferences, Work Style. Stored fields are unchanged.
- **Validation.** tsc clean; eslint clean apart from pre-existing warnings. Browser pane at 1280 with a fresh session: Play's first frame is the blurred veil, then the welcome; Profile and Connect open straight on their welcomes over a blurred page (scrim computed `blur(32px)`); Explore's welcome shows. Top 3 bands at 1280 show Investment Banking and Airline Pilot faces with their setting.

Now both columns measure their own position (scroll and resize, one frame at a time) and are exactly as tall as the room under them: `100dvh - top - 24px`, with top never less than the 117px pin. Measured at 1280x760 with the page at the top: reader bottom 736 of 760, and scrolling inside it reaches its last element. The scroll-into-place on open waits a frame so a reader opened from a link measures the laid-out page. Change them any time."

Nothing in the header changes. The reading layout is at least a viewport tall (minus nav and bar), so the page can scroll the title away on open and pin both columns under the filter bar at the full height. ### 2026-10-01 Explore: orientation without copy; one header on every device; the Schools bar fits

- **Why.** Chandu asked for orientation on Explore with no permanent copy and no coachmarks ("I don't want any permanent copy... lets not bring them back yet"), then: "how does a user know to press and hold for save?", "the schools, search, briefcase icons in smaller devices are guesses", and "why is investment banker not shown in the explore page until I search for it?"
- **What changed (orientation).** Posters carry a visible bookmark (`PosterSave` in `PosterCard.tsx`; Explore passes `saved`/`onSave` from the lab store), the same quiet glyph the School and Opportunity cards use, so saving needs no teaching. The first Browse row peeks sideways once (`dm-row-peek`) until any row is scrolled; the first For You card peeks up once (`dm-peek-up`) until the first swipe; both are `useDiscoveryNudge` flags, not copy. The For You card shows one tiny line above the title, "Because {career} is in your Top 3" or "Because you saved {career}", only when a same-world career exists (Chandu: "very tiny and short copy only"). No deck counter (the reel is unlimited), no icon labels on For You, no bottom-nav labels (Instagram has none).
- **Investment Banking** now leads the "Because you liked Business & Finance" row (`catalog.ts`, `BROWSE_BECAUSE_LIKED`); it was only reachable by search.
- **Bookmark on hover.** Chandu: "the save bookmark disappears on hover so it cannot be interacted with." The lifted poster had `z-index: 5` and covered its sibling save button, and moving onto the button dropped the card's own `:hover`. The wrapper (`poster-wrap`) now carries the hover: card and bookmark lift together and the bookmark rides the card's corner (`globals.css`).
- **One control family on every device (where this landed after four passes).** Chandu: "there needs to be a consistency with the tabs on different devices, don't switch places." Pass 1 copied the desktop lockup to phones (title, Careers/Schools text tabs, a pill with an icon over a 9px label): "this looks ugly, let's see how other platforms do it first." Survey: Instagram, TikTok and Pinterest use plain text tabs over the video; Apple Music, the App Store and Spotify use a 32px text-only segmented control; nobody stacks an icon over a label inside a segmented control. Pass 2: an Apple-style segmented control, then without the blue fill ("the highlight chip thing looks really bad"): a translucent grey track, a lighter grey selected segment, weight carries the state. Pass 3, the phone reel: no title, no Careers/Schools, just "For you / Browse all" as words over the video ("follow Instagram's UI there"), `ForYouBrowseToggle variant="text"`. Pass 4, phone Browse: "very cluttered with the two tab things competing... can we not just use icons for Careers/Schools on mobile?" One 36px row, no title: `ExploreSectionSwitch` (chrome.tsx) at the left, a compact segmented control in the same grey track where the selected segment shows icon + word and the other only its icon (briefcase for careers as Indeed, LinkedIn and Handshake do; graduation cap for schools), then For you / Browse all and Search at the right. Desktop keeps title + text tabs + the grey segmented control. `ForYouBrowseToggle` lives in `ExploreLab.tsx`; Schools and the component lab import it from there so there is one copy. The old phone row overflowed at 390px, which read as "the margins on mobile look really weird"; gone with it.
- **Row title and alignment.** "Because you liked Business & Finance", not "Recommended Because You Liked..." (Netflix's "Because you watched"; 8th-grade rule, say it once). Desktop rails now start their first card exactly under the row title (left inset = the page margin, right inset stays shorter so the trailing card still peeks past the margin line). The For You "Because you saved X" line from earlier today is removed ("we already show strong match etc.").
- **Schools filter bar between 1024 and 1280px.** Chandu: "the schools page is breaking" when the bar docks into the nav pill. Seven controls plus the count and Sort were wider than the pill there, and the row cannot scroll in that range (the panels would clip). `.dm-dense` (BrowseV2 row + `app.css`) drops the trigger icons, the count and the word Sort and tightens the trigger padding in that range only. Opportunities (four controls) was never affected.
- **Opportunities nav icon** is a rocket, not sparkles (Chandu: "the icon for the opportunities tab is bad"); sparkles read as magic/AI, a rocket reads as launch. Alternatives if it does not land: Ticket, Award, Target.
- **For You column no longer jumps.** Chandu: "the For you column keeps shifting with normal cards and videos, it jumps right and left." The desktop action rail (Save, Top 3, Like, Nope) rendered as an empty zero-width div on video cards, so the centred group narrowed by 56px and the reel slid 28px right and back. The placeholder now keeps the rail's 56px. Measured across six cards: the reel's left edge is 399px on every card, careers and videos alike.
- **Validation.** tsc and eslint clean. Browser pane: 1280 Browse (Investment Banking first, bookmarks on every poster, first row peeking, hover keeps the card lifted with the bookmark on its corner, title and first card both at x=56), 1280 For You (first card peeking, no Because line), 1024 and 1100 Schools (filter row fits the pill: scrollWidth equals clientWidth), 375 and 390 Explore Browse, For You reel and Schools (no horizontal overflow, one 36px header row, Instagram text tabs on the reel), 820 tablet Explore, Rocket in the bottom nav.

### 2026-10-01 Opportunities: a fifth tab for real scholarships and programs

- **Why a tab.** Joshua (30 Sept): a free scholarships API is coming, partners asked "where do you place the internships", and he lost them four taps into Connect (Communities, Finance, Updates). Options on the table were Explore sub-tabs (ChatGPT), a new Opportunities or Apply tab (Joshua), or Schools as its own top-level feature with scholarships and the Common App under it (Usman). The call: a fifth destination, because finding money and programs is neither "who am I" (Explore) nor people (Connect), it is information-dense (lists with deadlines, not reels), and My Plan already assigned the work ("Apply to 5 internships or programs", "Financial Aid & FAFSA Status") with nowhere in the app to do it. Schools stays in Explore so the Careers to Schools pairing is kept; Top 3 stays a Profile thing, so there is no schools list here (Chandu: "top 3 doesn't have to be in schools").
- **Why the name.** "Apply" reads like a CTA and "adds anxiety for a kid who hasn't decided anything"; "Earn" is "too grown up, 8th grader comprehension level". Opportunities is a school word kids hear from teachers, a noun, and already the type name for Connect's partner posts.
- **What it is** (`src/app/opportunities`, `src/components/opportunities/*`, `src/lib/opportunities.ts`). Read `docs/reference/schoolinks-scholarships-and-applications-notes-2026-10.md` for what was taken from SchooLinks' two walkthroughs and what was left.
  - Two lists, Scholarships and Programs (internships, summer programs, fellowships, competitions), with counts of what this grade can apply to. **Every record is real**, read from the provider's own page on 1 Oct 2026 (Chandu: "use real data to populate these tabs"); a fact the page did not state is null, never guessed. Partner posts come straight from Connect's Updates (`PARTNER_POSTS` adapter) under "Posted by", the SchooLinks "Posted by your district" pattern.
  - Fit is reasons, not a percentage: "Grade 11 can apply", "Open in New Jersey", "Fits your Top 3: Business & Finance", "Your 3.7 GPA is above the 3.3 needed"; things to check in amber. Grade from the demo student, state NJ (DEMO-ONLY), GPA from the profile, fields from the Top 3 picks.
  - Dates: "Closes Nov 13"; within two weeks it adds "in 9 days" in amber; when the provider still shows last cycle's date it says "Usually closes Nov 13" and the detail says so in words.
  - The filter bar is the Explore Schools dropdown kit, pulled out to `colleges/filterKit.tsx` (Closes, Field, Amount or Cost, Type, Grade, Sort). One row of removable chips, then the list on the left and the detail on the right; phones open the detail as a sheet.
  - Detail actions: Save, I applied (then "I got it"), Apply on {domain} (external, labelled). Undo after every change. Footer: when it was checked, "a real scholarship never asks for a credit card" (the counselor's own advice in the video), and "most money comes from the schools you apply to" with the way to Schools.
  - A season line per grade and tab; seniors get a FAFSA status (Not started, Started, Submitted) in the same three states the counselor's v3 Financial Aid screen uses.
- **Wiring.** Nav (desktop and phone) and quick links; Home's Next Moves has a fourth card; search has an Opportunities door; School detail has a Scholarships button beside Financial Aid (`?school=`); My Plan's "Apply to 5 internships or programs" is now IN APP and counts applications from the store (`studentSignals.programsApplied`), and both FUND steps link here.
- **Second pass, same day (design).** Chandu: "VERY TEXT HEAVY... progressive disclosure is key, information overload is the number one priority... title > subtitle > body top down everywhere... use logos... lead the eye along the story." The page now tells one story: the title and a single line ("9 open to you now. 24 more as a senior."); the filter bar (Closes, Type, Field, More, Sort), chips only when something is on; a two-column grid of cards built like Home's and Explore Schools' (glass surface, HoverBeam, the provider's mark, the money as a 26px hero number, the name, who gives it, when it closes, at most one fit signal); "Later" folded shut with one line on when it opens; the detail staged (mark, title, three facts, Apply first then Save and I applied, three reasons) with everything else behind Details. Every description, count line, season box and footer sentence that was not doing a job was cut. Logos: `OrgMark.tsx` uses the partner marks the repo ships (EY, JPMorgan Chase), otherwise the provider's favicon via Google's favicon service (DEMO-ONLY; only the provider hostname is sent), with a lettered tile as the fallback.
- **Third pass, same day.** Chandu: "I don't like the side view open by default... cards have to be clickable not just the text... things like Full ride are not the names of the scholarships, should they be chips? How is it usually done?... all of these pills look the same so they all compete for attention... don't do the side bar sheet, it's too narrow and sits very far on large screens... where are the internships tabs?"
  - **A page per opportunity** (`/opportunities/[id]`, `OpportunityDetailExperience.tsx`), the way a career and a school each have one; Back returns to the grid. Hero in the provider's own hue with its mark and the name in the display face; facts (award, closes, who can apply, when or renews); Fits you; Who it is for; What to bring; a sticky rail with Apply, Save, I applied, Undo; three More like this. No drawer, no sheet, no modal.

So `Preview.tsx`: nothing is open until a card is clicked; then the grid narrows to two columns and the preview sits beside it in the page flow (sticky, never fixed to the window edge, which is what made the drawer "sit very far" on wide screens): a band in the provider's own hue with its mark, the kind and the name, the award chip, two or three facts, Apply, Save, I applied, three reasons, Details, and a "Full page" link to `/opportunities/[id]`, which stays for deep links and the related rails. How can we do this without it going all transparent and illegible, but also not by making it a dark solid background by default?"; then "that's a black box and it floats on larger screens"; then "it should match with the navbar... they should work together... it should not have a gap, can it slot inside the navbar when scrolling somehow? Smoothly?" `StickyBar` (filterKit): at rest the row is transparent with its hairlines on the page column. A zero-height sentinel reports when it is actually stuck; then it takes the nav pill's own frost (62% background, 18px blur, glass border, same shadow), the pill's own width (the content column from lg; inset 12px from the viewport below lg, minus the scrollbar per the guardrails), bottom corners only (28px desktop, 22px phone), and sits flush under the pill at its measured bottom (68px desktop, 74px phone). It reports `setDocked` to chrome, and both pills square their bottom corners and drop their bottom edge, so the two read as one tall pill; everything transitions over 300ms. The controls move from the column edge to the pill's own inset as it docks. A sticky element only sticks within its parent's height, so the bar sits directly in `main` on both pages.
- **The preview is not a card.** Chandu: "the preview that opens should still have a more distinct UI, it still reads as a new card and it should have a close button." It now opens with a header strip that says PREVIEW with a labelled Close and the Full page link, a taller hero in the provider's hue with the name set in the display face (cards use sentence case; the full page uses this), a 24px radius against the cards' 16px, and a 1px outline in the provider's hue instead of the glass border.
- **The preview is a second pane, LinkedIn-style.** Chandu: "it's still just a card. It should look like a sidebar but not popping out like before... a second pane in the page itself, adjustable left edge, scrollable within the panel, but not separate like a sheet." On desktop the preview (`Preview mode="pane"`) is now an `aside` in the page grid: flat, no radius, a hairline on its left edge, it bleeds through the page's right padding to the viewport edge, starts under the docked filter bar (117px: the pill's 68 plus the bar's 49) and fills the viewport height, scrolls on its own with the PREVIEW header strip pinned, and shows the details open (the pane opening is the disclosure). Its left edge is a `role="separator"` drag handle (360 to 760px, arrow keys too), remembered in localStorage as a per-browser convenience. The card grid beside it uses auto-fill columns so it reflows as the pane is dragged. Phones keep the sheet.
- **Fifth pass: the reading layout, and one Saved.** After the drawer, the side-by-side card, the page, the in-row panel, the resizable pane and an expanding card, Chandu asked "what is objectively the best UX here?", tried the container transform, then: "let's not do the pop up modals, try the reading layout." So clicking a card switches the page to the Gmail / Apple Mail layout: the grid folds into a compact list on the left (`CardRow`: mark, name, who, award, date; the open row lit; a "Later, as a senior" divider), and the detail (`Expanded` in Preview.tsx) becomes the main surface on the right, in the page, sticky under the docked bar. Close returns to the grid; previous and next move through the list (arrow keys too); `?open=` names the open item. Phones show the detail alone.
  - **The detail's hierarchy:** the world band (mark, World · kind, the name in the display face, who gives it); a distinct action row (the award chip, Save, I applied, Apply); At a glance (closes, who can apply, when or renews, pay or based on); Why it fits you beside Who it is for; The award or The cost in the provider's words when the chip cannot carry it; What to bring; Dates; the checked-on footnote. Real section headings (15.5px bold) replace the uppercase micro-labels, which stay for fact labels only.

Every opportunity has a field; fields map onto the career worlds (`fieldWorld` in match.ts), and the worlds own a colour everywhere else, so the band is the field's world colour in PosterCard's own gradient recipe, and the eyebrow names the world. "Any field" gets the neutral surface. The full page uses the same band.

### 2026-09-26 Mobile taps no longer need two presses; For You actions move to the Reels/TikTok spot

- **Double tap on phones, fixed app-wide.** Report: "taps on mobile including the bottom navbar are taking two. One for like a hover interaction and one for the actual tap." Cause: after a tap, iOS Safari fires emulated mouseover/mouseenter first; if a handler changes the page (IconTip mounts its tooltip, which wraps every bottom-nav icon; HoverBeam lights its ring on almost every card), Safari treats the tap as hover and drops the click. Fix: a small inline script in `src/app/layout.tsx` stops emulated mouse events for 1s after any touch, before React's root listeners see them. Why a global guard and not per-component: it covers every existing hover handler (about 20) and any written later; a real mouse or trackpad never hits it. Also: `Tip` and `HoverBeam` open on focus only for keyboard focus (`:focus-visible`), so Android's focus-on-tap can't leave a tooltip stuck; the `dm-tap/quiet/link/chip-hover/solid` hover rules in `app.css` now sit in `@media (hover: hover)` so a card doesn't stay lifted after a tap.
- **For You actions on the right, lower (live Explore and the Career actions lab).** Report (iPhone 15 Safari): "why are the actions on the left?", then "should sit lower, mimic instagram and tik tok positions". The phone column used to be its own row above the details panel, wrapped in the Coachmark's `inline-flex` span, so it could shrink to icon width and land left. It is now absolute at the right edge, bottom-aligned with the caption, with the caption padded (`pr-[60px]`, lab `pr-[64px]`) so text never runs under it; desktop unchanged (`lg:`).
- **Summary/Details carousel stuck half way on iPhone.** Same screenshot showed both panels cut. The resting position was a pixel offset measured from the track width; a measurement taken before Safari finished layout stuck wrong. Now the track rests on a CSS percentage (0% / -50%) and the drag layer follows the finger then snaps back to 0 (`dragSnapToOrigin`).
- **Lab only:** the labeled column is lifted 10px so "Saved" doesn't crowd the CTA row ("the actions are however now colliding with CTA"); the phone Lab chip moved top-left, it sat on Play Game.
- Validation: `tsc` clean; checked at 393x852 and 393x660 in Chrome (live and lab), carousel chevron, drag and snap-back. Not verifiable here: real iOS Safari (no WebKit locally). Next: confirm on the iPhone that one tap opens bottom-nav items and cards.
