### 2026-09-25 Glossary Games: music was gated by the Sound toggle, not Music

**Why:** urgent report -- "sounds/music toggle is not working in the games, career simulations/glossary etc", then "an annoying beeping sound playing constantly", then the exact root cause named directly: "the music for glossary games is tied to the sounds button instead of the music button."

**What was actually wrong (`glossaryThemeSound.ts`):** the v2/v3/v4 background loop's per-note `AudioContext` getter was the *same function* used by the click/correct/wrong SFX, so scheduling a music note checked the Sound-mute flag (`isMuted()`) instead of the dedicated Music one (`musicMuted()`). Muting Sound silently killed the tune even with Music left on; the tune kept playing through a Sound mute whenever Music was on. Separately, the CRT (v2) theme's tape-hiss bed was a background noise node started once and only ever torn down by an explicit music-mute call or a theme switch -- once running, nothing re-gated it, so it could keep humming under a Sound-only mute (the reported "annoying beeping... constantly").

**The fix:** split the shared `AudioContext` into two gates -- `audio()` (SFX, Sound toggle) and a new `musicAudio()` (the loop, Music toggle) -- and made the loop's own `setInterval` tick re-check `musicMuted()` on every pass, tearing itself down immediately if muted from anywhere, not just when this module's own setter happens to be the one flipping it. The CRT hiss bed is removed entirely, per direct instruction ("take the static sound out completely") rather than re-gated, since it was the one thing nothing could reliably stop.

**Verified live** on `investment-banking`'s glossary game, v2 CRT theme: instrumented `AudioContext.prototype.createOscillator`/`createBufferSource` directly. Music (31 oscillators/4s) kept firing with Sound muted; zero oscillators fired within 4s of muting Music; zero `AudioBufferSource` ever created in any state (hiss fully gone). `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and `npx eslint` clean. Scoped to `src/components/play/glossaryThemeSound.ts` only -- career-simulation music (`music.ts`) already used its own independent mute key and was unaffected.

### 2026-09-25 Flow Lab: Mini Explore's scroll header fixed for real, scroll-reveal on cards

**Why:** the header/scroll pass in the previous entry shipped broken on first look -- direct reports: "lose the black bars everywhere... when I scroll down I can see the scrolling away things through the header," then, after a first fix attempt, "UGLY. Breaking the header treatment," and "use our loading states we design... let me see them."

**What actually broke:** the sticky sub-header used Tailwind's `bg-[var(--background)]/95` opacity-modifier syntax, which only works on raw RGB-channel custom properties -- `--background` isn't one, so the modifier silently no-opped and rendered fully opaque, a flat black slab with a hard seam against the fixed app header above it. The first attempted fix (`color-mix(...)` + blur) was applied to a bar still sized to the 880px content column via a negative-margin trick, which produced a floating slab with hard LEFT/RIGHT edges instead of a real header.

**The actual fix (`shared.tsx`'s `LabScreen`):** the sticky sub-header is now genuinely full-bleed (`w-full`, no side padding of its own, matching the shape `DesktopNavigation` in `chrome.tsx` uses for the site's real top nav), with its content re-centered to the 880px column *inside* it. It's always frosted (`color-mix(in srgb, var(--background) 78%, transparent)` + `blur(20px) saturate(1.6)`, no box-shadow) rather than scroll-triggered, because cards sit directly against it from the first scroll pixel on this screen -- a bar that's sometimes transparent right over dense photos is exactly the "scrolling things visible through the header" complaint. `FlowLab.tsx`'s own fixed app header keeps the site's real scroll-triggered frost (`useScrolled`, transparent at rest) since it sits above the sub-header, not over card photos directly -- confirmed transparent at scroll 0, frosted once scrolled, no seam against the sub-header below it.

**Scroll-reveal, per direct instruction ("when I scroll down things should load in with an animated transition"):** each `RevealGrid` card is now wrapped in a `motion.div` using the app's own scroll-reveal shape (`SchoolsIllustrations.tsx`'s `rise`/`VIEW`, scaled down for card size: `y: 14`, `duration: 0.45`, same ease curve), `whileInView` with `once: true` so a card animates in only the first time it scrolls into view, never on a re-render of cards already seen.

**Loading state, per direct instruction ("use our loading states we design"):** the infinite-scroll sentinel now shows the app's own `Working` chip (`src/components/app/Working.tsx`) instead of a bare spinner, per `docs/COMPONENT_STATES_PLAYBOOK.md`'s own default ("Skeleton loaders don't exist anywhere in this codebase yet... default to the `Working` chip").

**Also hit and fixed along the way:** a stray `Loader2` import removal left the dev server's cached bundle serving a reference error after the edit; `rm -rf .next` plus a genuinely fresh browser tab (not a re-navigate, which Chrome can serve from its JS cache) cleared it -- the running server was serving clean code the whole time, confirmed via a direct `curl` of the bundle.

**Verified live** on the dedicated dev server for this checkout at 1440 and 375: header transparent at rest, frosted and seamless once scrolled, no hard edges at any width; a card visibly mid-fade-in in a screenshot taken 80ms after a scroll jump, confirming the reveal actually animates; no console errors; no horizontal scroll on phone. `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` clean; `npx eslint` clean on both touched files.

### 2026-09-25 Counselor Dashboard v2: is the tool rail good UX, and a realistic centered document preview

**The rail question, answered honestly, not just defended.** Nested
left-side navigation (an app's own sidebar plus a page-scoped tool list)
is a common, well-established pattern -- VS Code's activity bar plus
explorer, Slack's workspace rail plus channel list, Notion's sidebar
plus page tree -- not automatically bad. Looking at the actual
screenshot: the app's own sidebar is the page's full-height frame (logo
top, account footer bottom, no border, spans the whole viewport height);
the tool rail is a bordered card scoped to the page content, starting
and ending with it, well short of the viewport. They already read as
different things structurally. The one real remaining risk: both used
an identical active-row treatment (tinted pill, primary icon), which
could still read as duplicated nav at a first glance. Fix: a small
"TOOLS" header label above the rail (`ProductivitySuite.tsx`), the same
device Slack and VS Code use for exactly this. Cheap, standard, removes
the ambiguity without adding a new visual language.

### 2026-09-25 My Profile: Preferences tab (Joshua's spec, ported from his reference)

**Why:** Joshua Pierce, Slack, 25 Sept 2026: counselors supporting 300+ students need to read a student's interests, careers, education and school preferences in one place and see whether the Career Report and My Plan line up with them; students "complete Build once and may feel like those answers are permanent. They need to be able to update them anytime." Reference: dceeai.replit.app/my-profile#preferences, walked section by section (every editor, every option list) before building.

**What:** a sixth Profile tab, `?tab=preferences` (`src/components/profile/PreferencesTab.tsx`), eight section rows with the current answers and an Edit sheet each, in the reference's order and copy: Career Focus (industries max 3, careers max 3), Subjects (max 5), Work Style (how you like to work, pace, structured/flexible, team size max 2, environment max 3), Education (GPA + type, pathways max 2), Location & Cost (states max 3, distance, tuition budget), School Experience (type/setting/size, max 2 each), Skills & Software (what I want to build next max 5, suggested for the student's first career from the data the app already holds: Career Report skills, career profile goodAt/software, Explore's software list, the Match deck; plus Skills I have / Software I know behind a fold), Internships & Jobs (Optional; opportunity types, roles max 3 suggested from the career, locations max 3, work mode max 2, and graduation year / availability / relocate / languages / certifications / portfolio behind "More job preferences"). Chips carry "n of max selected" and disable at the cap, as in the reference. Every string is the reference's (direct instruction after the first pass: "keep the content of copy exactly the same as replit"); the two Work Style groups that are in the Slack spec but not the reference (structured/flexible, work environment) are left out of the sheet and kept in the store. Only the limits differ where the spec is explicit (5 subjects, 5 skills to build; the reference showed 3).

**Data (`src/lib/preferences.ts`):** `dreamari-preferences` in localStorage, same store idiom as `studentProfile.ts`. First read SEEDS from Build (interests, subjects, GPA and type, states, distance, path) and from Match (the Top 3 become "careers I'm considering"), so the tab is never empty for a student who did Build. Saving WRITES the overlapping answers back to the student profile (industries -> interests, subjects, GPA, states, distance, pathways -> path), so Match, the Flow Lab and school matching follow. `MAX_INTERESTS`/`MAX_SUBJECTS` in `studentProfile.ts` went from 2 to 3 and 5 so the store stops truncating what Preferences allows; Build itself still asks for two. Also: an explicit `?tab=` now wins over the first-visit Overview tour (the tour used to force Overview even for `?tab=plan` links).

**Interaction audit of the reference (after the first push; direct question: "did you go through his replit and click on everything?"):** clicked every chip, cap, fold and Save. Findings and what we do: (1) Save closes the sheet, shows a green banner above the rows, "Saved. Your recommendations will update.", and bumps the date -> added, same copy, gone after 4s. (2) At the cap his chips grey out (`disabled:opacity-40`); ours swap the oldest pick instead, which is Build's own rule (24 Sept 2026: locking picks out "creates friction"), kept deliberately. (3) His "Suggested for" is hardcoded to Investment Banking even after it is removed from the careers; ours follows the student's first named career. (4) His careers list does not change with the industries; ours adds the catalog careers of the chosen worlds after the Top 3 and saved ones. (5) On phones his rows show only the chevron and the editor is a full-height sheet -> "Edit" hidden below sm, our sheet is 92dvh from the bottom. (6) Chip hover in his build is a faint accent tint; ours is Build's chip (dm-tap). Still open from the Slack spec and absent from his build: structured/flexible, work environment, "preferred industries max 3" under jobs (fields exist in the store for the first two).

**Verified live** (own dev server on :3005, since :3000 is the counselor worktree's): tab appears sixth; rows seed from a Build profile ("Business & Finance · Tech & Engineering", "3.7 GPA · 4-Year College", "NY · NJ"); Career Focus editor shows the seeded industries pressed, careers from the Top 3 and the chosen worlds; Save updates the row, "Last updated", `dreamari-preferences` and the student profile; Skills editor says "Suggested for Data Scientist" with that career's real skills and software; Jobs editor expands the extra fields. `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` clean; eslint clean on the new files. ### 2026-09-25 Counselor Dashboard v2: the school year map, seeded mid-year progress, and the Vercel build fix

Three direct reports in one message: "i see empty graphs in overview etc please seed data so that this doesn't happen"; "where is the grid or whatever you said you wanted to steal from SchooLinks? Please make every update to make this better. Please don't make it too similar to SchooLinks where it looks like a copy"; "a previous deployment failed because of a build error or something. Please check".

**Deploy failure (fixed).** Vercel rejected 76911d7f while the same commit built locally. The Vercel log: `Module not found: @vercel/turbopack-next/internal/font/google/font` / `next/font/google queries have exactly one entry` on `bricolage_grotesque`, which is exactly the Vercel-only Turbopack failure `src/components/marketing/fonts.ts` already documents and worked around with a `<link>`. `src/components/build/fonts.ts` was the last `next/font/google` Bricolage call in the repo (MatchLab, MatchGrid, Build's steps, WelcomeScreen, DreamyGuide). It now exports `{ className: "font-display" }`: the root layout's font `<link>` already loads Bricolage 400/600/700/800 on every route and Tailwind's `font-display` resolves to that family, so every call site is unchanged and there is no build-time font resolution left to fail. `npm run build` passes.

### 2026-09-25 Flow Lab: Top 3 fits the viewport, the detail modal is Match's, honest reason chips, (i) notes and the hamburger

Four direct reports in one sitting, each fixed at the cause:

- **"These cards get cropped by the bottom. This should never happen. Make them responsive height-wise so a scroll is not necessary."** The Top 3 grid used fixed poster ratios inside a viewport-high section. `TopThreeScreen` is now two layouts: on desktop three columns whose poster takes whatever height is left (`min-h-0 flex-1` wrapper, card `absolute inset-0`), on phones three compact rows (thumbnail, title, the four actions, Replace and Remove as icon buttons with tooltips) that share the leftover height. The swap list opens as an overlay on the card so it never adds height. Verified: `scrollHeight === innerHeight` at 1440 and 375.
- **"I don't think we're showing all the information that was there on the opened card detail as we have in the actual Match that is canon today."** Correct. The lab modal had two thin sections. `DetailModal` now mirrors Match's `DetailModal` section for section: employers chip, salary chip, "What You'd Do", "Good Fit If You Like", "School & Path" as 2-3 bullets, "Details coming soon." when unauthored. `matchDetail()` in `lab.ts` supplies it: the deck's own copy for the six deck careers (verbatim), otherwise the Career Report (glance, responsibilities, common education, majors, median, employers), then the career profile (summary, scenario, goodAt, typical degree, studies, typical pay), then the resolved detail. Verified: Data Scientist shows the deck's exact bullets and "Google · Meta · almost every industry" / "$120K median".
- **"The chips that say fits mathematics for everything need to say different things. What's the idea here?"** The chip was the first Build answer that matched, and the Mathematics keyword list was broad enough (engineer, data, architect) that every Tech card matched it. A first fix showed the part of the world the title implied instead, which was rejected in the same sitting ("the chips should be relevant to the recommendations, not random"): a chip must be the student's own choice, not something inferred from the title. So the chip is now only a matched subject ("Fits Mathematics") or the matched path ("College path"), no chip when nothing matched, and the subject keyword lists are narrow (Mathematics no longer claims engineer/architect/data; Computer Science gained database/systems/computer). Cards that match come first, so the six a student sees are the ones that fit what they told Build, with the chip naming which answer.
- **"Give me a rundown of what we built from Joshua's notes, how we tried to improve his version, a disclaimer for v3 and the reason behind it, and say these are mocks, not final designs. Put these in (i) buttons subtly in the top right."** `notes.tsx`: `FLOW_NOTES` per version (v2: built from the note as written, what we added without changing the flow, mock not final; v3: the flow, why this shape against the survey findings, disclaimer) and `InfoSheet`, opened from an `InfoButton` in the header. Short bullets, no em dashes.
- **"Make sure he can navigate to other flows etc with the hamburger with the quick links too."** The header now carries the app's own `QuickLinksMenu` next to the (i), so the demo, the counselor dashboard and the lab itself are one tap away from inside the lab.

### 2026-09-23 For You card swipe: fixed a real "gets stuck" bug -- imperative spring-back instead of a declarative `animate` prop

Direct report: "i can swipe left on the first slide and it goes and gets stuck, they should snap back to their original state if i swipe the wrong way." (Landed right after the tablet width-cap fix above, same session, same carousel.)

**Root cause**: the carousel used `<motion.div animate={{ x: face === "Summary" ? "0%" : "-50%" }}>` -- a DECLARATIVE target. Dragging "the wrong way" (e.g. swiping right while already on Summary, which has no previous slide to go back to) doesn't change `face`, so the `animate` target's VALUE is literally identical before and after the drag ends. Framer Motion resuming control of a motion value after a `drag` gesture releases it isn't guaranteed to re-run a spring purely because the prop *object* re-rendered with an unchanged target -- there's no new value to animate TO, so nothing visibly happened: the panel stayed wherever the raw drag left it. That's the "gets stuck."

**Fix**: switched from the declarative `animate` prop to an imperative one. `x` is now a real `useMotionValue(0)` bound directly via `style={{ x }}` (Framer's own recommended pattern for exactly this). A new `settleAt(face)` helper calls `animateValue(x, target, spring)` directly, where `target` is computed from a LIVE measurement (`carouselTrackRef.current.offsetWidth / 2` -- half the track's real rendered width, since the card's actual width differs by breakpoint). `onCarouselDragEnd` now ALWAYS calls something: past the swipe-commit distance it sets `face` (which a `useEffect` picks up and calls `settleAt`), short of it (in EITHER direction) it calls `settleAt(face)` directly right there in the handler -- there is never a code path where a drag ends and nothing explicitly commands `x` to a real resting position.

One side-effect fix bundled in: `dm-swipe-nudge` (the one-time "you can swipe this" wiggle) was on the SAME motion.div as the new `style={{x}}` binding -- a CSS `transform` keyframe animation and a Framer-driven `transform` on the identical element fight each other. Moved the wiggle to the outer non-Framer wrapper div instead.

Verified live at 820x1180 (tablet) with real drag-simulated gestures in all four combinations: Summary swipe-forward (commits to Details), Details swipe-backward (commits to Summary), and both "wrong way" cases (swiping further past either end now visibly springs back to the same face, confirmed via screenshot each time -- no stuck/misaligned state). Also re-checked 375x812 (mobile) for regressions. `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and `npx eslint` clean.

### 2026-09-23 For You card: real finger-following swipe (Framer Motion), timed progress fill, one-time swipe nudge, bigger chevrons

Two rounds of direct correction on the same interaction, worth recording together since the second reworked the first's approach entirely:

1. **Swipe did nothing on touch.** The hand-rolled pointermove/pointerup threshold detector (added earlier the same session) lost the gesture mid-drag on real touch devices -- any genuine finger swipe drifts vertically a little, and without `setPointerCapture` the browser could hand the in-progress touch off to native scrolling and stop delivering events to it. First fix added capture + `onPointerCancel`; live testing then surfaced the deeper ask underneath the bug report.
2. **"The slide should move with my finger, not just switch... when i swipe."** A threshold-based detector, however reliable, can only ever fire once at the end -- it can't make the panel visually track the pointer per frame. Replaced the whole hand-rolled system with Framer Motion's own `drag="x"` on a real two-panel carousel (Summary and Details side by side in a row twice the container width, each panel exactly half that row, so `x: "-50%"` shows the second one). `dragElastic={0.22}` gives resistance past either end; `onDragEnd` commits past `SWIPE_COMMIT_PX` (50px) or springs back to the current face otherwise via the controlled `animate` prop; a plain tap (negligible drag distance) still fires a normal click that bubbles to `flipFace`, since Framer doesn't suppress the click for a drag that never crossed its own activation distance. The old CSS-grid opacity-crossfade technique (`col-start-1 row-start-1`, `aria-hidden` + `opacity-0`) is gone; `aria-hidden` alone stays on each panel for screen readers, since the flex row's own height-to-tallest-child behavior already keeps the panel height constant the same way the grid stacking used to.

**Progress track now fills in real time, not full-the-whole-time-then-flip.** Direct instruction: "they can fill up along with the seconds so its not full the whole time... track progress according to how long they are visible." Each segment gets a genuine CSS `width: 0% -> 100%` animation (`dm-progress-fill`, `app.css`) running for `AUTOPLAY_MS` (6000ms, the same constant the real autoplay `setTimeout` uses) while ITS face is the active one, keyed on `` `${face}-${active}` `` so leaving and re-entering a face (which always passes through `active` going false first) remounts the span and restarts the fill in lockstep with the real timer -- no extra state needed to track this (an early version used a separate incrementing `useState` counter bumped inside the timer effect, which `eslint`'s `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` correctly flagged as a cascading-render anti-pattern; deriving the key from existing props/state instead of new state sidesteps it entirely). Details' segment fills the same way even though there's nothing further to auto-advance to -- a static, already-full segment read as "nothing is happening here" against Summary's filling one.

**One-time swipe nudge**, since "its not understood that i can swipe or tap anywhere" was the original report this whole interaction started from, and no caption is allowed to say so (standing instruction: no new copy on the card). `dm-swipe-nudge` (`app.css`): a small horizontal wiggle (translateX 0 -> -18px -> +12px -> -5px -> 0) on the carousel itself, gated on the same `useDiscoveryNudge`/`hasInteracted` first-view flag the rest of this card's nudges use -- motion teaches the gesture instead of words.

**"Strong match"'s shimmer/spark is now permanent, not gated on the discovery nudge** -- direct instruction: "should always be playing, dont make it disappear after the first thing." Different from the swipe-hint wiggle above (a one-time "learn this" cue) on purpose: this one is just a permanent shine on the card's one evaluative label, unconditional `dm-text-nudge`/`dm-nudge-spark`.

**Chevrons bigger below `lg:`** (32px hit target, 16px icon vs the prior 16px/12px) -- direct instruction: "the chevrons can maybe be bigger on tablet too so i can tap them." `lg:` keeps the tight desktop size since a mouse doesn't need the extra hit area.

Verified live at 375x812: a real drag-simulated swipe (not just a click) correctly commits Details -> Summary and back. `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and `npx eslint` clean (after fixing the set-state-in-effect error above).

### 2026-09-23 Explore For You card: real swipe + paced autoplay between Summary/Details, redesigned scrim, hierarchy and legibility pass

Direct request, following a round of artifact mockups reviewed and iterated together: the For You reel card's tap-to-flip (Summary <-> Details) wasn't discoverable ("its not understood that i can swipe or tap anywhere"), and a string of follow-up corrections landed the final design. Recorded here as one entry since the corrections built directly on each other in the same session.

**Interaction**, `EnvCard` (`ExploreExperience.tsx`):
- Real swipe added alongside the existing tap-anywhere-to-flip, via pointer handlers on the panel (`touchAction: "pan-y"` so the reel's own vertical swipe-between-cards still works underneath -- only a drag whose horizontal movement dominates counts as a face-swipe).
- Auto-advance Summary -> Details after 6s on screen (`active` + `face === "Summary"` gated, one-directional only -- doesn't loop). 6s, not the first draft's 4s, per: "people need time to read first dont be too fast."
- The old two-dot indicator replaced with a short, fixed-width progress track + small chevrons, pinned to the panel's FAR LEFT -- deliberately as far as possible from Like / Not for me / Save (which live in their own row above the panel and were explicitly NOT to be moved: "those are from instagram tik tok etc so its familiar").
- First-view discovery nudge via the existing `useDiscoveryNudge` (`src/lib/nudge.ts`) + `dm-nudge-spark` -- but as its own small decorative spark icon beside the chevron, not applied to the chevron itself. First attempt put `dm-nudge-spark`'s class (its own scale+rotate keyframes) directly on the chevron button, which visibly spun it -- "the left chevron... seems to be tilting and rotating."
- The whole panel's `dm-tap` (hover lift + drop shadow, meant for a discrete card/button) removed -- "should not hover/lift and drop shadow... just a layer there."

**Type hierarchy**: field labels (Median Salary/Major/Main Skills) and the match-quality kicker were first sized SMALLER than their own values (10px label under 13px value) -- direct correction: "heading>subheading>body... eyebrow... smaller than the info" inverted the actual rank. A subheading must be sized BETWEEN the heading and the body it sits between, not below the body. Relabeled/resized to 14px labels (still muted/dim for reading emphasis) over 13px bright values -- size carries structural rank, brightness carries which text the eye should actually read first. The redundant "MORE INFO" kicker on the Details face was dropped entirely (the progress row already says which face is open).

**Scrim/blur**: `ProgressiveBlur`'s lightest layer had nowhere to fade from -- its band started at the panel's own top edge (0%), so the blur onset read as a hard line right where the panel began, worse once the new progress row added ~20px of panel height. Fixed by extending the blur's own container 130px above the panel (`PROGRESSIVE_BLUR_REACH`), entirely into the photo, clipped by the card's own overflow-hidden -- the existing feathered-mask math now has real room to ramp. Added a subtle extra dark tint band inside the same masked container (per "if the progressive blur needs a little more dark tint that's okay, subtly") and lightened `LEGIBLE_TEXT_SHADOW` from two stacked shadows to one, since the tint now carries more of the legibility job ("don't make it look like we overindexed on shadows").

**Details face layout**: Details has less content than Summary (no title/description of its own), but the grid cell sizing (both faces stacked in one cell, sized to the taller sibling, so toggling never changes panel height) meant Details' shorter content top-aligned and left a dead gap before the CTA row. Added `justify-center` to the Details cell so that gap splits evenly instead of dumping it all at the bottom ("keep the height constant... align the text in slide 2 so it doesn't look like it has awkward empty space").

**CTAs**: `Play`/`Eye` icons removed from Play Game/More Info (text only now), text size 16px -> 17px.

**Action buttons** (Like/Not for me/Save): added a drop-shadow filter to the icon itself when floating bare over the photo (not the non-bare surfaced version elsewhere) -- Instagram/TikTok's own fix for the same problem, background-independent unlike a background chip.

**For You | Browse All toggle** (`ForYouBrowseToggle`): the boxed/bordered pill is now `lg:`-only. Below that (mobile AND tablet, where this toggle sits directly on the reel's photo) it's plain text again -- bold+bright when selected, dim when not, a text-shadow for legibility -- per: "restored to what it was for mobile before... just text like instagram with a subtle scrim and shadows." The desktop version (a normal page header, not over a photo) keeps the bordered glass pill.

Verified live at 375x812 (mobile), 820x1180 (tablet), and ~1100-1600px (desktop framed card) -- swipe, tap, chevrons, autoplay pacing, hierarchy, blur gradient, toggle style and CTAs all confirmed at each width. `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and `npx eslint` clean throughout.

**Follow-up, same day -- three real bugs caught by direct testing after the first pass landed:**

1. **Content jumping between faces.** The kicker span (Strong match / More Info) was conditionally UNMOUNTED for Details rather than hidden, so its line-height dropped out of the flex column and everything below it (the grid, the CTAs) shifted up the instant Details opened -- exactly what "constant panel height" was supposed to prevent (direct report: "the content in both slides keep jumping around"). Superseded anyway by the next point, but worth recording: conditional rendering and conditional visibility are not interchangeable when height must stay fixed.
2. **"Strong match," always, both faces, brighter white, with the nudge.** Rather than juggle a hidden-on-Details kicker, simplified to always showing `career.matchLabel` on both faces (direct instruction: "what if we have strong match on both slides"), which also resolves point 1 outright (same element, same position, every time -- nothing to jump). It now also carries the discovery nudge (dm-text-nudge sweep + dm-nudge-spark twinkle, same pattern as ForYouBrowseToggle's "For you" label). Color went through two rounds: first the app's own green "GOOD" token (`var(--world-food-farming-nature)`, same one MentorshipTab.tsx uses) since it's the one evaluative label on the card, not a neutral fact like Major/Main Skills -- then a direct follow-up asked for plain white instead, just brighter than those field labels rather than a new hue on the card ("maybe it can [be] white but just slightly brighter than what major and main skills are"), landing on `rgba(255,255,255,0.88)` vs their 0.62. One more small fix on top: `dm-text-nudge`'s `background-clip: text` technique makes the glyphs' own fill transparent, so the panel's inherited text-shadow was painting underneath that transparent fill as a dark smudge rather than behind solid text ("the sparkle shimmer... also add[s] a dark overlay on the text") -- fixed with `textShadow: none` on just that nudge-active span.
3. **`ProgressiveBlur`'s reach, tuned three times against real measurements, not guesses.** First pass (130px) fixed the hard-line-at-the-panel's-own-top-edge bug but reached so far up it visibly softened Like/Not for me/Save above the panel ("blurring the action buttons... shouldn't be too tall"). Measured live: the real gap between Save and the panel's top is ~32px on a phone, so reach came down to 24px to respect it. That alone still read as a faint line ("still read as a sharp line ever so slightly") because the mask math itself was flawed independent of reach: `bandStart = index/total` always put band 0's target at literal 0% of whatever box it's in, and `Math.max(0, bandStart - feather)` always clamps a 0%-target's feather window to zero width -- a genuinely instant transition no amount of external headroom actually fixes, just relocates. Changed to `bandStart = (index+1)/total`, giving every band (including the first) an equal, non-degenerate feather window; also toned the blur stops down (max 35 -> 30) and the extra dark tint down (0.22 -> 0.16 opacity) per the same follow-up ("the blur can be toned down ever so slightly too... everything's still visible"). Confirmed clean live: no line, Save/Not for me/Like all sharp, gradient reads as one continuous build.

`npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and `npx eslint` clean after each of the three; re-verified live at 375x812 after the final round.

### 2026-09-23 Build flow: fixed three more zoom-compounding double-scale bugs (map screen, Welcome mascot, GPA picker dialog)

Direct report, Chrome, wide desktop: "the map screen in build requires scrolling on larger screens... It shouldnt. Please fix and apply a universal fix for all browsers. Only tablet/mobile are allowed to scroll." Same root cause as every other instance of this bug class fixed this month: this app's own wide-screen zoom system (`globals.css`, `zoom: 1.1`/`1.25` past 1441x800 / 1800x900 via `--vz`) double-scales any raw `dvh`-based size, or any `position:fixed`/JS-positioned element, that sits inside the zoomed tree -- the value is already true post-zoom pixels, then the CSS engine multiplies it by `zoom` again on paint. Confirmed via `getComputedStyle` (local, pre-zoom) vs `getBoundingClientRect()` (real, post-zoom) on each element before fixing.

Three fixes, one root cause:
1. **`LocationStep.tsx`** (the map screen) -- the map SVG's `max-h-[clamp(150px,calc(100dvh-470px),44dvh)]` was double-scaled (measured 384.12px local vs 422.5px real = exactly x1.1 at zoom 1.1), so the map rendered taller than its allotted space and forced the whole screen to scroll. Wrapped the whole clamp in `/ var(--vz, 1)`.
2. **`WelcomeScreen.module.css`** (Dreamy mascot on the first Build screen, which this file's own pre-existing comment already says must "fit without scrolling") -- 6 raw-`dvh`-in-`clamp()` instances for `.dreamyStage`/`.dreamy` sizing (base rule + two `@media` breakpoints) had the same bug. Same fix, `/ var(--vz, 1)` on each.
3. **`GpaField.module.css`** (`.dialog`, the GPA picker popover) -- the more serious one. First attempt only divided `max-height`, matching the pattern used for the two fixes above; live re-measurement caught that this was incomplete -- the dialog's POSITION was also double-scaled: it's a native `<dialog>` shown via `showModal()`, and even though that promotes it to the browser's top layer, it still inherits ambient CSS `zoom` from its ancestors (confirmed live, was previously an open question). `--picker-left`/`--picker-top` (`GpaField.tsx`) are set from a real `getBoundingClientRect()` -- already true screen pixels -- so `left: 970px` meant to sit flush with the GPA field instead rendered at a real 1212.5px (970 x 1.25, at zoom 1.25), drifting the whole popover away from the field that opened it. Reverted the max-height-only fix and applied `zoom: calc(1 / var(--vz, 1))` to the entire `.dialog` rule instead (same technique as the landing mascot's stage, `Mascot.tsx`) -- cancels ambient zoom on both position and size together so they can't drift apart from two separate corrections. `max-height` reverted back to a plain `calc(100dvh - 32px)` since the whole-element zoom cancellation already covers it.

Verified live at both zoom tiers: 1920x873 (zoom 1.1) and 1920x920 (zoom 1.25) for the map; GPA dialog re-measured after the fix at zoom 1.25 -- `dialogRect.left`/`top` now match the trigger's real position and the JS-set target exactly (970, 383.625 -- previously drifted to 1212.5). `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` clean; `npx eslint` clean on `LocationStep.tsx` (the two `.module.css` files have no ESLint config, expected -- CSS isn't lintable by this project's ESLint setup).

One caveat worth recording since the ask was "universal... for all browsers": the fix uses CSS `zoom`, which is WebKit/Chromium-originated and not yet a formal CSS standard, though broadly supported (Chrome, Edge, Safari) and already the established pattern this app uses everywhere else for this exact bug class (Hero.tsx's mascot, this same file's own comment history). Not flagged as a blocker -- consistent with existing app-wide precedent.

### 2026-09-22 Glossary Games shell: width and height now scale together on tablet/desktop, anchored to a MacBook Air "home base"

Direct ask: the central Glossary Games shell (`GlossaryGameExperience.tsx`) was 1:1/desktop-sizing-never-done -- `<main>` (and the header progress strip) were hard-capped at `max-w-[640px]` while every `dvh`-based `clamp()` inside it (TermFlipCard, SpeechBubble, UnlockScreen, QuestionScreen's prompt) scaled purely off viewport HEIGHT. The two axes were never tied together, so a tall+wide screen kept growing text/icons toward their height-driven max while width stayed pinned at 640px (and vice versa on a narrow+tall screen) -- the same class of bug `globals.css`'s `--match-card-size` comment already documents for Build's MatchCard ("nothing tied the two dimensions together").

Fix: one new CSS custom property, `--glossary-shell-scale`, defined once on the component's own outer wrapper (same place `--glossary-accent` already lives), multiplied into every previously-hardcoded width (`max-w-[640px]` x2, the question/answer card's `620px`, and every intro/unlock/complete screen's own content-wrapper width) and into all 12 `dvh`-clamp text/icon sizes via `calc(Npx*var(--glossary-shell-scale))` -- one shared driving value instead of width and height moving independently. `FeedbackPanel` and `StreakModal` (fixed overlay modals, not part of the shared `<main>` shell) were deliberately left untouched.

**Went through two rounds of direct correction on the formula itself, worth recording so nobody re-derives this from scratch:**
1. First pass anchored growth at 640x800 (`clamp(1, min(vw/640, dvh/800), 1.4)`) -- floored at 1 for phones, grew only slightly past 1x elsewhere. Rejected: "keep the macbook air screen (ours as a benchmark) and scale up from there proportionately and down proportionately... I think it's still too small on wider screens."
2. Second pass re-anchored to 1440x900 (a 13" MacBook Air's own CSS viewport) as the true "1x, not scaled" home base, using `max(widthRatio, heightRatio)` so a window that's only taller than the anchor (not wider) still grows -- `min()` would have frozen that case at a flat 1.0 forever. Still rejected with a screenshot: a pure ratio only grows as fast as the viewport does (39% wider viewport -> only 39% bigger content), which reads as barely different on a genuinely large monitor -- "theres so much space that the modals can use."
3. **Landed formula**: `clamp(1, min(calc(1 + max(calc(max(0px, (100vw - 1440px)) / 750px), calc(max(0px, (100dvh - 900px)) / 750px))), calc(100vw / 640px)), 2.2)` -- additive beyond the anchor (every 750px past 1440 width or 900 height adds a full extra 1x of scale, whichever axis is ahead), which grows noticeably faster than the viewport itself. A separate `100vw / 640px` term is `min()`'d in purely as an overflow guard (640 being the largest base width this scale multiplies, so if `<main>` never exceeds the viewport, nothing smaller does either) -- it only binds in a genuinely narrow-but-very-tall edge case, never at any real test size. Floors at exactly 1 for phone/tablet-below-the-anchor, so mobile is provably byte-identical (checked live: `<main>`'s computed `max-width` and the SpeechBubble's computed `font-size` matched the pre-change formula's output to the pixel, not just visually).

Verified live (`/play/glossary/investment-banking`, `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and `npx eslint` clean throughout):
- 375x812: `--glossary-shell-scale` floors to exactly 1; `<main>` max-width = 640px and SpeechBubble font-size = 22.736px, both matching the pre-change formula exactly.
- 768x1024: scale ~1.165, `<main>` max-width ~746px, mild growth.
- 1440x900 (the anchor): scale = 1 exactly, `<main>` max-width = 640px -- genuine unscaled home base.
- 1920x1080: scale ~1.64, `<main>` max-width ~1050px, no horizontal overflow.
- 1440x1600: scale ~1.93, `<main>` max-width ~1237px (comfortably under the 1440px viewport), no horizontal overflow -- confirms the tall-but-not-wider case still grows.
- 2000x1100 (an extra check after the "still too small" screenshot, specifically re-testing IntroScreen/DreamyIntroScreen/LessonIntroScreen, not just the question card): IntroScreen's own card max-width = 838.4px, up from a base of 480px.

Cross-browser guardrails self-check: this file doesn't touch scrollbars, native OS controls, `getBoundingClientRect()` positioning, or `title=` tooltips, so only the `tsc`/`eslint` item applied (clean).

Committed as `4f3e3ead` (along with relocating the demo-only background-version chip off the top bar into a new bottom-center `DemoControlsDock`, same commit, done separately).

**Follow-up same day**: direct correction with a screenshot -- "THE CTA Buttons dont need to stretch past a respectable amount, just the MODALS and their internal elements like text, images, buttons, chips etc need to scale proportionately in locked aspect ratio and not just extending to the side with no visual QA." Every CTA button (`<button>`, not a content wrapper) had been using the exact same `max-w-[calc(Npx*var(--glossary-shell-scale))]` pattern as the card/text around it, so at the top of the scale range a button like "Next" or "Unlock Company" grew just as wide as its card -- a "stretched pill," not a normal CTA.

Fixed at each of the 7 CTA buttons that carry their own scaled max-width (IntroScreen's Next, DreamyIntroScreen's Start Learning Finance, LessonIntroScreen's Start Lesson, UnlockScreen's Unlock, UnlockCompleteScreen's Start Practice, PowerPlayIntroScreen's Unlock & Test My Knowledge, CompleteScreen's Continue): `max-w-[calc(Npx*var(--glossary-shell-scale))]` -> `max-w-[min(calc(Npx*var(--glossary-shell-scale)),560px)]`. 560px clears every screen's own historical CTA base (480/520/440/420/380px) so the cap never binds below the 1440x900 anchor -- mobile/tablet CTAs stay exactly as they were. Everything else (cards, text, images/icons, option chips/pills) was deliberately left alone, still scaling fully with the card, per the same feedback ("everything else... should keep scaling together with the card"). The "Check Answer" / "Check My Sorting" / "Check My Math" buttons inside the question/answer card were checked and left alone too -- they're plain `w-full` filling their own already-correctly-scaled card, not carrying an independent scaled max-width of their own, so they were never part of this bug.

`npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and `npx eslint` clean. Verified live (not just computed pixel values -- actually screenshotted and eyeballed per the "no visual QA" callout):
- 375x812: button max-width still exactly 480px (IntroScreen's Next) -- the 560px cap doesn't bind below the anchor, unchanged from before.
- 1920x1080: IntroScreen's card max-width 787.2px, its Next button capped at 560px -- button now visibly narrower than the card above it, reads as a normal CTA.
- 1440x1600: UnlockScreen's card ~1197px (TermFlipCard, large and proportional), its Unlock Company button capped at 560px -- clearly narrower than the card, no longer a stretched bar. No horizontal overflow.
- 2000x1100: UnlockCompleteScreen's card 733.6px, Start Practice button capped at 560px -- same well-proportioned result.

**Follow-up same day (second round)**: direct correction -- "the glossary game central modals, flip cards etc all of that can scale vertically a bit more too. Theres so much space left blank and it feels like the actual game content and questions and answers seem like theys it too low. Please compose it better. The flipcard/card/surface should be central." Two separate bugs, both in the shared `<main>`/outer-wrapper shell so the fix applies to every screen at once, not per-screen:

1. **Vertical centering was systematically biased low.** Root cause: `DemoControlsDock` (see above) is `position: fixed`, so it takes zero space in the flex column -- `<main>`'s own `justify-center` was centering its content against the FULL remaining viewport height as if the dock weren't there, while the dock visually covers real pixels at the bottom. Confirmed live before the fix: at 2000x1100 the question card's true center sat at y=592.5 against a TopBar-to-dock-top free area centered at y=555.25 -- a 37px low bias. Fixed by measuring the dock's real on-screen footprint (`dockSpace`, via a new shared `useMeasuredSpace` hook + `ResizeObserver`, not a hardcoded constant -- its rendered height turned out to vary by viewport, 36px at 1440x900 vs 44.5px at 2000x1100) and adding that as extra `padding-bottom` on `<main>` (on top of, not replacing, its normal `--space-4` padding), so `justify-center` centers against the space a viewer actually sees. Re-measured after: card center within ~3-8px of true free-area center at every tested size (0px exactly at 1440x1600).

2. **Not enough vertical growth on wide-but-not-very-tall monitors.** `--glossary-shell-scale`'s growth was `max(widthGrowth, heightGrowth)` -- on a monitor like 1920x1080 or 2000x1100 (width well past the 1440 anchor, height only modestly so), the ENTIRE scale was driven by width alone; height's own smaller growth term was discarded rather than contributing. Changed to `widthGrowth + heightGrowth` (both added), which raised exactly those cases (2000x1100: 1.75x -> 2.01x pre-safety-guard; 1920x1080: 1.64x -> 1.88x) while leaving the anchor and the pure-height 1440x1600 case unchanged. Cap raised 2.2 -> 2.6 to give this room.

That stronger growth immediately surfaced a THIRD, genuinely new bug: a height-overflow, not just width-overflow. At 2000x1100 with the bigger scale, UnlockScreen's own stack (heading + term-count label + TermFlipCard + Unlock button -- the tallest of any screen's composition) grew taller than the space actually available, pushing the Unlock button to y=1113-1184 (past the 1100px viewport entirely) and forcing real page scroll (scrollHeight 1365 vs clientHeight 1100) -- exactly the overflow this whole effort exists to prevent, just vertical instead of horizontal. Fixed with a height-overflow guard mirroring the existing width one: `--glossary-shell-scale` now also `min()`s against `(100dvh - var(--top-bar-space) - var(--demo-dock-space) - 32px) / 650px`, where `650px` is UnlockScreen's own measured content height at scale 1 (forced `--glossary-shell-scale: 1` live and measured heading-top to button-bottom, +32px for the screen's own padding, rounded up slightly for margin), and `--top-bar-space` is the top bar's real measured height (also live-measured via the same `useMeasuredSpace` hook, not hardcoded -- it turned out not to be fixed across viewport widths either: 60px at 1440 wide vs 75px at 1920/2000 wide, reason not fully tracked down but the live measurement makes the exact cause moot).

`npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and `npx eslint` clean (one intermediate `react-hooks/refs` error -- mutating a ref during render while building the shared measurement hook -- caught by lint itself and fixed by moving the assignment into its own effect, before this was ever reported as done). Verified live at every required size, checking actual centering and overflow, not just that a formula's numbers matched:
- 375x812 / 768x1024: unchanged -- `<main>` still exactly 640px / 745.8px, SpeechBubble font-size still exactly 22.736px on phone, no overflow.
- 1440x900 (anchor): still exactly 640px, unscaled, now also correctly centered (previously sat slightly low even here).
- 1920x1080: card grew to ~894.5px (height-guard capped it below the ~1.88x the growth formula alone would have wanted, correctly -- no overflow), centered within 8px of true free-area center.
- 1440x1600: card unchanged at ~1237px (height guard never binds here -- plenty of vertical room), now PERFECTLY centered (0px difference, was previously off).
- 2000x1100: card ~914px (height-guard bound here too), Unlock button back on-screen with no page scroll, centered within 8px.

### 2026-09-22 App-wide bug: IconTip's own `relative` silently beat callers' `absolute` positioning

Direct report on Match's grid: "The content inside the 6 cards in match are
getting cropped and overlapping and messed up layouts" -- confirmed live and
via `getBoundingClientRect`: the card's own "+"/rank select button (passed
`absolute top-2 right-2` through `IconTip`'s `className` prop) was landing
at its plain in-flow static position (top-left-ish, on top of the salary
chip) instead of the card's top-right corner, at every viewport size,
mobile through wide desktop.

Root cause, in `IconTip.tsx`'s own `Tip` component: its wrapper `<span>`
always carries a hardcoded `relative` class, and when a caller ALSO passes
`absolute` (or `fixed`/`sticky`) through `className` to position the whole
trigger, both classes land in the same `class` attribute with identical
CSS specificity (0,0,1,0 each) -- so whichever one Tailwind's generated
stylesheet happens to list LAST wins the cascade, not whichever the caller
"meant." In this project's build that was `relative`, silently overriding
every caller's own positioning. This is not Match-specific: `grep`
confirms it affects **every** `IconTip` call site across the app that
positions itself via `className="absolute ..."` -- close buttons on
`ProfileExperience.tsx`, `ConnectExperience.tsx`, `CommunityCard.tsx`,
`MentorshipTab.tsx`, both AT&T Connect views; mute/save/close on
`CompanyVideoCards.tsx`; the dismiss control on `NextStepBanner.tsx`;
Explore's video mute; the trailer's mute button; Match's own carousel
prev/next arrows in the detail modal, in addition to the select button.

Fixed at the source rather than patching each call site: `Tip` now only
adds its own `relative` when the caller's `className` doesn't already
carry a position utility (`/\b(?:absolute|fixed|sticky|static)\b/` test),
so a caller's own `absolute`/`fixed` positioning is never fought over.

`npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and `npx eslint` clean. Verified live on
`/match-grid`: all six cards' select buttons now sit correctly in their
own top-right corner (confirmed with `getBoundingClientRect` -- zero
overlap with the salary chip, ~9px from the card's right edge, at both a
normal viewport and the 1800x1000 wide-desktop size that triggers the
app's own 1.25x proportional zoom), tapping one still saves/highlights/
shows its "Remove from Top 3" tooltip correctly, no console/server errors.
Did not exhaustively re-verify every other affected screen live (time),
but the fix is structural and this class of Tailwind conflicting-utility
bug is deterministic -- every other call site gets the same correction.

Next step: push (explicit go-ahead: "Fix and push" pattern this session).


### 2026-09-22 Play tab's row-focus: hovering back to row 1 did nothing on a large screen

Relayed report: "Jish showed me his play tab he has a large screen on
chrome. THe glossary games row scales up and does its job but when he
hovers back on the first row it doesnt hover or scale up, basically it
doesnt work."

Root cause: `PlayHub.tsx`'s row-focus ("TV UX" -- one row hero-sized, the
rest compact, Netflix/Apple-TV remote-nav style) is driven ENTIRELY by
`useCenteredRow`, an `IntersectionObserver` watching which row crosses a
thin band across the vertical center of the viewport -- i.e. by SCROLL
position, not by the mouse. That's deliberate and correct for touch (no
hover exists there at all), but on a large screen where the whole page can
already fit without scrolling, moving the mouse back over row 1 doesn't
generate any scroll/intersection change for the observer to react to --
there's simply no signal telling it row 1 is active again, so it stays
stuck on whichever row last actually scrolled into the center band.

Fixed by giving a real mouse hover its OWN, higher-priority signal rather
than routing it through scroll: `PlayHub` now keeps a `hoveredRow` state
that overrides `useCenteredRow`'s scroll-derived answer whenever it's set,
via `onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave` on each row's own `data-row-id` section
(`rowHoverProps`, guards against a stale leave from the row you're moving
AWAY from clobbering the enter of the one you're moving INTO). Scroll
behavior for touch/keyboard is completely unchanged; a mouse now claims a
row immediately on hover instead of needing an actual scroll to happen.

`npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and `npx eslint` clean. Verified live at a
1800x1100 viewport (no page scroll needed to see every row) by dispatching
real `mouseenter`/`mouseleave` sequences matching Josh's exact report --
hover Glossary Games (confirmed via its heading turning the accent color)
-> hover back to Career Simulations without any scroll in between ->
confirmed BOTH the heading color AND the actual hero/compact card sizing
swap back correctly, screenshotted before/after.

Next step: push (go-ahead given after reporting the fix: "Yes please").

### 2026-09-21 (cont'd) v2/v3/v4 corrected against their actual live references, several rounds of tuning

The previous round's v2/v3/v4 (commit `f0d9642b`, pushed) were built from written descriptions of their references without actually loading the live demos. Once compared side by side against the real thing, all three needed real rework -- not committed yet, this is all local.

- **v2 (CRT) was rejected outright**: "The crt is bad, nothing like the reference... Please have HUD, UI and everything more like the reference, like an OLD TV." Actually opened `codepen.io/creme/pen/aPJwEz` this time (a fresh browser tab got past a permission block an earlier tab had hit) and read its SCSS directly: the reference uses a hard **4px** scanline band (`background-size: 100% 4px`, not a faint 1px hairline), a `.noise` layer whose **opacity itself animates** (not just the texture), and an RGB-split glitch **text-shadow** animated in `steps(9)` through several saturated color offsets, on a `#2b52ff` blue screen. Rebuilt `PlayBackdropV2Crt.tsx` and `globals.css`'s CRT keyframes around those real values (kept black, per the earlier still-standing "not blue" instruction), then iterated through several more corrections, in order: **scanlines invisible** ("this is just a noise pulse") -- root cause was the noise layer's `mix-blend-screen` sitting ON TOP of the scanlines and washing out their contrast; fixed by reordering (noise first, scanlines painted after) and raising alpha; **pulsing glow too fast/strong + lines too thin** -- slowed the noise flicker (3s -> 6s, dimmer range) and widened the scanline band (4px -> 8px); **glitch text scoped wrong, twice** -- first applied broadly (screen headings + the question prompt bubble), corrected to "not the questions and answers, slowly glitch the HUD elements not text," then corrected AGAIN to drop HUD text entirely too ("glitch the graphical elements only") -- landed on a `box-shadow` RGB-split pulse on the filled mastery dots specifically, nothing else, at a slow 3.5s ease drift; **background too flat/dark** -- added two magenta/cyan tinted radial glows (same palette as the glitch effect) instead of flat `#000`, per "Use a better color & gradient for the background. We want more color than dark."
- **v3 (Dots) was rejected outright** too: "the v3 dots are bad. Heres the actual reference for it" (vantajs.com/?effect=dots). Actually loaded it this time: Vanta.DOTS is a **scattered** (not gridded) field of small dots at varying sizes, connected to nearby neighbors by thin lines (`showLines`), where the whole scene **pans with real camera parallax as the pointer moves** -- not individual dots flying anywhere, which is what the previous "hyperspace warp" attempt did (itself a correction of an even earlier "static glowing grid" that had no motion at all). Rebuilt `PlayBackdropV3Dots.tsx` a third time to match: a jittered-not-gridded scatter, a proximity line network between nearby dots, a spring-eased whole-field parallax offset following the pointer, and a very slow per-dot drift so it's never perfectly frozen.
- **v4 (Synthwave)**: corrected before ever being shown live -- "the synth one should be exactly like its reference, remove the round sun thing in the background and apply perspective: make sure the grid colors match the background colors." `WebFetch` on the codefronts.com reference page gave real technique/color values (`perspective: 340px`/`perspective-origin: 50% 0%`/`rotateX(78deg)`, a single magenta grid color from the same family as the sky gradient, `background-position` animation instead of a translated strip). Sun removed entirely. One more tuning pass after: "Slow down and also make the synth grid more transparent and thinner. Its too distracting" -- scroll slowed 1.4s -> 4s, lines 2px -> 1px at roughly a third the opacity.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and `npx eslint` clean across every touched file after each round. Verified live: cycled all three again end to end after the final tuning pass -- CRT scanlines now clearly visible with a colored (not flat black) base, Dots now reads as a connected constellation with pointer parallax instead of a static grid or a warp tunnel, Synthwave has genuine converging perspective with no sun and a subtle grid.

### 2026-09-21 (cont'd) Glossary background v2/v3/v4 experiments, behind a version chip

Direct request 21 Sept 2026: "Now lets work on v2,v3,v4" (the roadmap outlined earlier this session: v2 CRT/retro matching the CodePen reference sent previously, v3 a Vanta.js Dots effect, v4 a retro synthwave grid horizon, "color match to complement the background" for all three). v1 (Stars + berry backdrop) stays the shipped default; the other three are opt-in via a demo-only chip, same idea as Connect's AT&T v1/v2.0 toggle.

- **`src/components/play/PlayVersionChip.tsx`** (new): a small `role="tablist"` of 4 buttons in `TopBar`, `?bg=2/3/4` opens straight into that experiment (state lives in `GlossaryGameExperience.tsx`'s `bgVersion`, read on mount and written back via `history.replaceState`, mirroring `att/VersionChip.tsx`'s exact pattern).
- **v2 -- `PlayBackdropV2Crt.tsx`**: black CRT scene (kept black, not the CodePen reference's blue tint, per the earlier direct instruction) -- scanlines, an animated SVG-turbulence static layer, a curvature vignette, a slow flicker, all recolored to the game's own gold accent as the phosphor color instead of the classic green. "Match UI, cards, fonts" handled without rewriting every component: the root wrapper adds a `play-crt` class only when this version is active, and `globals.css` scopes token overrides under it (`--font-display` -> `"Courier New", monospace`; `--card`/`--glass-border` -> near-black with an amber edge) -- every card/heading in the file already reads those same tokens.
- **v3 -- `PlayBackdropV3Dots.tsx`**: a Vanta.js "Dots"-style scene, built first-party (a canvas grid, each dot's size/brightness driven by a slow ambient wave plus pointer-proximity glow) rather than adding the `vanta`/`three` packages for one background. Dots recolored to the game's own gold.
- **v4 -- `PlayBackdropV4Synthwave.tsx`**: a CSS retro grid horizon -- a striped sun (gold-to-magenta gradient, masked into horizontal bands), a starfield sky, and a `perspective()`/`rotateX()` grid floor in magenta/cyan.
- **Two real color bugs found and fixed while building these**:
  1. **`useResolvedColor` was resolving to the wrong color** -- it appended its measurement probe to `document.body`, but `--glossary-accent` is set as an INLINE style on the game's own root wrapper, so a probe outside that element's subtree never saw it and silently fell back to body's own inherited text color. Invisible in `FireworksBackground`'s usage (white was already one of its 5 palette colors, so a wrong-resolves-to-white bug blended in), but immediately obvious in `PlayBackdropV3Dots`'s single-color dot field -- confirmed by sampling actual canvas pixel data (`(236, 240, 243)`, near-white, not gold). Fixed by appending the probe inside `.marketing-v2` (the class every screen that sets this token also carries) instead of `document.body`.
  2. **The `.play-crt` token overrides were losing the cascade** -- `tokens.css`'s own `.marketing-v2 { --font-display: ... }` is the exact same specificity as a bare `.play-crt { }` rule, and source order put it after this block, so v2's font/card overrides silently never applied. Fixed with a compound `.marketing-v2.play-crt` selector (both classes are always present together on the root wrapper), which is unconditionally higher specificity.
- **`SpeechBubble` swapped its literal `#151829`/`#f4f2fa` colors for local custom properties** (`--speech-bubble-bg`/`--speech-bubble-fg`, same literal defaults) so `.play-crt` can retint it too, without reopening the light-mode bug those literals were fixing in the first place (still never reads `var(--card)`/`var(--foreground)`, which flip with the theme toggle).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .`, `npx eslint`, and `npm run tokens:check` all clean across every touched/new file. Verified live: cycled all four chip options end to end (intro through a mid-lesson screen on v4, the busiest of the three new scenes) -- CRT scanlines/static/vignette/monospace-and-amber cards, gold Vanta-style dots with visible pointer glow, and the synthwave sun/grid/starfield all render correctly, and game content stays fully legible over all three.

Next step: get this pushed; further polish on any of v2/v3/v4 (the synthwave grid's perspective convergence reads a little flat and could use more tuning) whenever asked.

### 2026-09-21 (cont'd) Stars Background + Fireworks on success screens, backdrop rebalanced to berry, HUD text bigger

Resumed the backdrop experiment after the checkpoint below, per "Then lets get back to experimenting." Two new animate-ui components pulled in (both via read-only `npx shadcn@latest view @animate-ui/...`, never `add` -- see the entry below this one for why), several real bugs found and fixed along the way, all live-verified.

- **`src/components/ui/stars.tsx`** -- animate-ui's Stars Background (`@animate-ui/components-backgrounds-stars`), adapted (no `cn`, `framer-motion` instead of the separate `motion` package). Wired into `PlayBackdrop` as the main scene's motion layer, recolored to this game's own wash via its `background` prop, `starColor="#ffffff"` for contrast. Its own `useEffect`+`setState` random-position generation was replaced with a seeded PRNG computed in `useMemo` -- avoids both a server/client hydration mismatch (the original's whole reason for deferring to an effect) and this repo's `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` lint rule. `speed` raised from the reference's default 50 to 140 after "Slow the movement of the stars upward... please."
- **`src/components/ui/fireworks.tsx`** -- animate-ui's Fireworks Background (`@animate-ui/components-backgrounds-fireworks`), adapted (no `cn`; no `motion` dependency at all, this one's pure canvas). Wired into the two full-screen "success" moments, `UnlockCompleteScreen` and `CompleteScreen` (direct instruction: "use this on success screens, color match to UI"):
  - **Color-matching needed a real color, not a CSS variable** -- canvas `fillStyle`/`strokeStyle` can't parse `var(--glossary-accent)` directly (canvas draws outside the CSS cascade). Added `useResolvedColor()`: a hidden probe `<span>` gets `style.color` set to the CSS expression, and `getComputedStyle(probe).color` reads back the fully-resolved `rgb()` -- `color`, unlike a custom property, resolves its whole `var()` chain through `getComputedStyle`. The `setState` call is deferred one `requestAnimationFrame` tick to satisfy the same lint rule as the stars fix.
  - **Real sizing bug, found via the DOM**: passing `className="... absolute inset-0 ..."` to `FireworksBackground` merged with its own hardcoded `relative` base class in one string -- both `position` utilities landed in the class list, Tailwind's cascade order (not DOM order) picked a winner, and the container collapsed to zero height, so nothing ever drew. Confirmed live via `getBoundingClientRect()` (`height: 0`). Fixed by wrapping in a dedicated `<div className="absolute inset-0 z-0">` that owns the positioning, leaving `FireworksBackground`'s own base classes untouched inside it.
  - **Real stacking bug**: the fireworks wrapper (`position: absolute`) was painting IN FRONT of the screen's ordinary in-flow text/cards, not behind them -- a positioned element with `z-index: 0` still paints above non-positioned content by default (direct instruction: "make sure the fireworks happen behind the content UI"). Fixed by wrapping the actual content (badges, trophy card, score card, buttons) in its own `relative z-10` group on both screens.
  - **Color rejected twice**: first pass was `[accent, "#fff7e6"]` (gold + near-white) -- "color them dont just make them white." Widened to a real 5-color palette (`[accent, coral, magenta, yellow, white]`); the magenta swapped from an initial teal to `#ff3d9a` once the backdrop went berry (below), so the fireworks read as "of the same world," not clashing.
  - `PlayBackdrop` gained a `showStars` prop so the two success screens run fireworks-only, no stars underneath ("do not combine the fireworks with the star background use only the fireworks"). **Found a real bug wiring it**: the `Screen` type has an `"unlockComplete"` member that is never actually assigned anywhere -- `UnlockCompleteScreen` renders as a sub-case of `screen === "unlock"` once `unlockIndex` reaches the term count, not a distinct screen value, so the first `showStars={screen !== "unlockComplete" ...}` condition silently never matched. Fixed to check `screen === "unlock" && unlockIndex >= lesson.terms.length` directly.
- **Backdrop palette changed twice more**: jade/emerald (from the checkpoint below) read as "still feels black dominated... try a different combo than green/yellow" -- rebuilt on a berry/magenta palette (`rgba(219,39,119,...)`/`rgba(157,23,77,...)` glows over a `#2a0a1f`→`#170a14`→`#3a0f2c` floor) with much bigger, stronger glow radii so color genuinely dominates the frame instead of two small accents on mostly black. Still fixed (not accent-derived), still clear of the app's blue/purple family and the CTA's own gold.
- **HUD text bumped up**: the in-question status strip (lesson title, fraction/percent, "Mastered X/Y", mastery dots) was deliberately shrunk in an earlier round ("make the progress bar info smaller") -- superseded by "the HUD text size can be bigger, match it to the career simulation HUD sizes." Sized to match `SimulationPlayer.tsx`'s own `Hud` (13px title line, 11px secondary line); mastery dots grown from 16px to 20px to stay proportionate.
- **Investigated, not a bug**: "the circles under the progress bar dont seem to fill up" -- traced `creditedTermIds`/`mastery` end to end; each term genuinely needs **two** correct answers before its dot fills (`MASTERY_TARGET = 2`, existing by design, Duolingo-style). Confirmed live: one correct answer to "What is a company?" correctly left the dot unfilled and "Mastered 0/5" unchanged.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and `npx eslint` clean on every touched file throughout. Verified live end to end after each fix: stars visible and slowed, fireworks correctly sized/behind-content/colorful/stars-free on both success screens, berry backdrop with far more color coverage, larger HUD text, mastery-dot behavior confirmed intentional.

Next step: push this round (see the still-open push note below); the v2 (CRT/retro), v3 (Vanta dots) and v4 (synthwave grid) toggle variants the user outlined are explicitly deferred to their own round, not started this pass.

### 2026-09-21 IB Level 1 location coverage + drag-rank fix, Glossary game redesign, profile cover self-heal, Explore Play-badge fix

- **`locations.ts` had a stale routing comment** ("SimulationPlayer routes every non-card, non-review beat straight past this table to the plain ambient backdrop, on purpose") that turned out to be false -- `sceneFor()` never gates on beat kind, and Level 2/3 and the nursing sim already give every beat a room, art-owning beats included, as a fallback for once their own art goes stale. Level 1 was the only level missing this (built the same session, following that comment). Mapped every remaining Level 1 beat id to its act's room; only the terminal review beat stays unmapped, same as every other level. Corrected the comment itself. Verified live: the rapid-fire and drag-choice beats that previously showed the flat gradient now show their dimmed room.
- **RankBody (the drag-to-reorder beat) was silently double-applying every reorder**: `onPointerUp` called `setRows(...)` as a side effect inside `setDrag`'s own updater function, and React 18 Strict Mode double-invokes updaters to catch exactly this kind of impurity. Two passes of the same splice through the already-shifted list is not idempotent -- depending on drag distance it either nets back to the original order (reported live as "it snaps back") or lands scrambled. Reproduced deterministically by scripting real PointerEvents against the DOM and matching the corrupted output to two sequential `reorder()` calls exactly. Fixed by reading `drag` directly in the handler and keeping `setDrag(null)` separate and side-effect-free. Verified live: a 1-slot and a 2-slot drag both land exactly where dropped now.
- **Glossary Game (`GlossaryGameExperience.tsx`) redesign**, direct feedback on screenshots (page and the feedback popup both read as flat/boring on near-black, question content sat low with a large empty gap above it, progress info too dominant, Unlock required two taps per term against the reference's one): swapped the custom near-black tint for `AppBackdrop` (the same app-wide layered purple/blue/teal wash + starfield every other screen already renders), explicitly NOT the Replit reference's own palette (corrected mid-session after an initial pass copied its color stops) -- built from this app's own tokens only, with the career's accent glow layered on top. Question screens now sit directly under the progress strip instead of centered in the leftover space below it; the strip itself shrunk and quieted. Unlock screen: removed the required flip-to-reveal (`SketchFace` deleted, along with the now-orphaned `playFlip`/`RotateCw`), term/definition/example show immediately in the same ring-bound card, Unlock stays the one action that advances. - **Profile cover image, reported broken live on Vercel** ("loads, then slowly does something else, then I see [the browser's broken-image icon]"): the mount-time guard in `ProfileExperience.tsx` only rejected a `blob:`-prefixed stored value (a leftover from the since-removed upload feature, `df96e809`), so any OTHER stale/invalid value -- a renamed file, anything unrecognized -- still passed through with nothing to fall back on. Replaced the blocklist with an allowlist (only an exact match against the known `COVERS` set or the career sentinel is trusted; anything else is purged from storage, same as "nothing saved") and added `onError` self-heal on both cover `<img>` layers so any future bad value (including a broken top-career poster path) falls back to the default cover instead of showing a broken icon, and stops persisting once corrected. Verified live: seeded a stale `blob:` value, reloaded, cover renders clean and localStorage now holds a valid path.
- **Explore reel card's "Play Game" button had no `onClick` and no check** for whether the career actually has a simulation (confirmed bug from the engineer's Slack feedback, 20 Sept) -- it rendered on every card in the "For You" reel regardless. ### 2026-09-19 Corner bleed fixed at the root, resume label color matched, Messages tab shows notifications + the conversation, tablet stacking restored

- **Corner bleed, real root-cause fix**: `CardProgressiveBlur` (cardChrome.tsx, shared by many pages) only put `border-radius: inherit` on its own OUTER wrapper span, not on each individual `backdrop-filter` blur-stop span inside it. Chromium can promote a backdrop-filter element to its own compositing layer and clip it before the ancestor's radius is baked in, leaving a hairline sliver of the unblurred edge visible right along the curve -- confirmed by comparison against `PosterCard` (same border/rounding, no backdrop-filter, no artifact). Each blur-stop span now carries `border-radius: inherit` itself. This fixes it everywhere the shared component is used, not just the three prep cards. A separate, unrelated attempt (wrapping the blur in an extra clipping span) broke the blur outright and was reverted before this fix.
- **Resume label color**: was defaulting to `accent` (Coach's tan) while Explore/Play use `WORLD_COLORS`, two different colors for what reads as one eyebrow treatment. Resume's `PrepFoot` now passes `tone={WORLD_COLORS[D.PREP_CAREER.world]}`, matching its siblings exactly.
- **Messages tab, launch path made explicit**: an "Open" conversation row now sits at the top always, and a "Waiting on you" section below it lists any message-related notifications (the existing meeting-proposal entry, Accept/Decline included) using the same `Row` component every other tab uses -- direct feedback: "I should see message notifications and the conversation which I can click to open... otherwise how do I launch messages?"
- **Tablet stacking**: reverted back to `lg:grid-cols-2` (full width through 1023px, side by side from 1024px) after a brief `md` experiment that reintroduced the earlier squeeze.
- Checked headless: blur confirmed present via computed `backdropFilter` values (6 stacked layers up to 34px) after an earlier false alarm from a stale browser tab; corner hairline visibly fainter at 3x zoom on all three cards; tablet (768px) confirmed stacked, not side by side; Messages tab dialog text confirmed showing both the Open row and the meeting notification with Accept/Decline. tsc and eslint clean (one pre-existing unused-var warning).

(`src/components/connect/primitives.tsx`): IBM, Genentech, CDC Foundation,
UnitedHealth Group, Kaiser Permanente, Moderna, Warner Music Group,
Paramount, Condé Nast. Their "+N more" chip in `CommunityCard.tsx`'s
`MoreMarks` popover was falling back to plain text for all nine.

Sourced a real SVG mark for each (mostly Wikimedia Commons, trimmed to ink

these again:

1. **CDC Foundation** is the independent nonprofit, not the government CDC

   Wikimedia's CDC seal. The source file's "Together our impact is greater"
   tagline (fill `#85888b` in the original) was stripped out of the SVG,
   keeping just the dot mark + wordmark.
2. **Warner Music Group's source had a real bug for our system**: the "W"
   ribbon shape is a cutout achieved by painting an opaque white rect BEHIND
   an opaque blue path with the ribbon as a hole -- fine for normal
   rendering, but our `CompanyChip`/`CompanyMark` mask to a single ink color
   off the alpha channel, and alpha doesn't care about z-order/color, so the
   whole square came out as a solid blob. Fixed by deleting that backing
   rect so the ribbon is real transparency. **If a future mark looks like a
   blob instead of its icon, check for this same pattern** (an opaque
   "background" shape sitting behind a shape that's supposed to read as a
   hole).

### 2026-09-07 (later still) Schools view: replaced the sticky stage story with plain rows, rebuilt Connect, dropped pill CTAs

Several rounds of direct feedback in quick succession:

1. "Doesn't work properly when scrolling" -- the five-stage section used a
   sticky right column whose composition crossfaded on an IntersectionObserver
   timer while the copy scrolled past on the left. A stage's copy could sit
   far from the frame showing a DIFFERENT stage, and each copy block's tall
   min-height left large dead gaps between consecutive stage headers.
   Replaced with plain, non-sticky alternating rows (`StageRow`): each
   stage's copy and its own card sit side by side in normal document flow,
   so they can never desync -- removed the IntersectionObserver, the
   `active` state, and the sticky column entirely. (Introduced and fixed a
   bug in the same edit: `Reveal`, a `<div>`, was wrapping each `<li>`
   instead of sitting inside it, producing invalid `ol > div > li` markup
   that also broke `divide-y` and any `ol > li` query -- moved `Reveal`
   inside `<li>`, one per column, verified `ol > li` count is 5 again.)

2. Connect's card: rebuilt as a photo-plus-solid-modal composition (like
   HeroVisual/ProgressArt) per direct instruction, dropping the `Frame`/
   `Product`/`zoom` machinery entirely for this one -- `CommunityCard` is a
   real `@container`-responsive component that sizes itself, not a fixed-px
   screen needing a scaling hack. Three follow-on bugs from that rebuild,
   each reported immediately and fixed in turn: (a) proportions were off --
   capped at max-w-300px while every other stage's card rendered near

### 2026-09-07 (later still) Schools view: de-nested the stage frames, minimized Build's questionnaire, fixed the copy/frame misalignment, made the Connect overlap real

Four rounds of direct feedback, same session, on the five-stage "Five steps
toward a clearer future" section and its composed visuals:

1. "Frame inside frame inside frame" on Build/Match/Explore/the data section.
   Root cause: `SchoolsVisuals.tsx`'s `Product` component painted its own
   bordered, shadowed, rounded-corner dark box, nested inside the outer
   `Frame` that already draws that exact chrome one level out -- two visible
   boxes where one was intended. `ProgressArt` and `HeroVisual` never had
   this problem because their `Product` floats over a plain photo with no
   enclosing `Frame`. Fix: `Product` takes a new `bare` prop that drops its
   border/shadow/rounded-corner/background, used everywhere a `Product`
   already sits inside a `Frame` (Build, Match, Explore, the data section);
   `ProgressArt`/`HeroVisual` keep the default chrome, unchanged.
2. Build's card was "such a tall graphic," "everything visible at once":
   `BuildArt` passed all 15 `INTEREST_WORLDS` to the real `ChipGrid`, an
   8-row grid at near-full design scale. Fixed by showing a 6-option preview
   (both of the two "selected" worlds included) -- the same "6 visible, more
   below" convention the app's own `ChipGrid` already uses for phones
   (build/ui.tsx, PREVIEW=6), just applied here so the composed snapshot
   reads as a glimpse, not a rendered-out list.
3. "Alignments are off, badly designed": the section heading sat right above
   the sticky frame's top edge, but each stage's copy was vertically
   *centered* inside a 76vh-tall block (`lg:justify-center`), so "01 BUILD"
   rendered roughly 38vh (well over 300px on a typical laptop) below the
   heading while the frame started right under it -- two starting points a
   half-screen apart. Changed to `lg:justify-start` with a short top pad and
   a shorter 62vh block, so each stage's copy anchors near the top of its
   slot, close to the sticky frame at every stage, not just visually
   accidental for whichever one happened to scroll into the "active" band.
4. Connect's two cards: earlier this session they went from overlapping-and-
   illegible (bug, fixed to a flex-column with a real gap) to fully
   separated with no overlap at all. Direct feedback: the overlap itself was
   wanted back -- "liked the overlapping components... just don't make them
   so transparent that they overlap and get mixed." `Card` is the app's real
   frosted-glass surface (backdrop-blur, ~90% opacity) -- correct where it
   sits over a plain background, but stacked over ANOTHER card that blur
   reveals and blends the card underneath into it. Fixed by reintroducing a
   real overlap (negative margin, not independent absolute boxes) with an
   opaque backing plate the exact shape of `Card` sitting behind it and in
   front of the community card, so the blur terminates on solid colour and
   nothing shows through.
