## 2026-09-28 · College networking requests (demo)

**Why.** Harvard team feedback via Joshua: college students want to network 1:1 with professionals, but on LinkedIn they cold-message people who never signed up to help. Dreamari's volunteers did sign up, so a request can be structured (Follow first, one message, real student context attached) and bounded (a weekly allowance), instead of an open inbox that could overwhelm a volunteer. Flow: Follow -> prepare in Dreamari -> send ONE request -> the volunteer Accepts or Declines -> a conversation opens.

**DEMO-ONLY College POV toggle.** A small segmented control on the professional profile (`PovChip`, `src/components/connect/networking/pov.tsx`), styled like the Resume Builder's own v1/v2 chip and switchable via `?pov=college`. High School is the default and unchanged (Follow, public boards, no messages). College reveals the Message panel below the header. This is a page-local override, deliberately separate from the app-wide `dreamari-stage` flag (`src/lib/stage.ts`) that mentorship and other features already gate on, so this feature could be demoed without touching that flag's meaning elsewhere.

**Student side** (`StudentMessaging.tsx`, embedded in `ProProfileView`): Message is disabled with a plain-language reason until the student follows the pro. Once following, a composer (reusing `Composer` from `primitives.tsx`) lets them send one request with a real activity line attached. While pending it shows "Request sent · waiting for {name}"; once accepted it shows an inline conversation; a decline lets them try again. The allowance line ("3 of 3 networking requests left this week") sits under the composer with a link to Play.

**Weekly allowance** (`src/lib/networking.ts`): 3 base requests, up to 4 more earned from real Dreamari activity (every 3 completed simulation levels or 5 completed glossary levels earns one, hard capped at 7 total). Derived from `studentSignals.ts`'s existing `simulationsCompleted`/`glossaryLessonsCompleted` counts rather than re-parsing `dreamari-play-progress`/`dreamari-glossary-progress` a second time; enforced in the store (`sendRequest`), not only in the UI, so nothing routes around it. Reset is keyed to the calendar week (Monday-start).

**Pro side** (`ProRequestsPanel.tsx`, a new "Messaging" tab in `ProDashboard.tsx`): a messaging setting (Open to requests / Paused / Public only), an incoming-requests list with the student's college year, career interest, one real activity line (e.g. "Finished Investment Banking simulation, level 3", derived from the actual play/glossary progress stores, `describeRecentActivity()`), and their one message -- so Accept/Decline is never a blind decision. Accept opens a minimal conversation thread inline; Decline needs no reason. Seeded with 3 realistic requests against `pro-okafor` (Investment Banking, the default dashboard pro and one of the two playable simulations) so the panel isn't empty on first load; tagged `demo: true` in the store.

**Conversation** (`Conversation.tsx`): a small bubble-row thread with its own composer, shared by both sides. Deliberately NOT a fork of the mentorship program's chat dock (`mentorship/MentorshipTab.tsx`) -- that component is wired to its own ongoing-program data shape (scheduling, session history) that this single-accepted-request feature doesn't have; forking it would have carried UI this feature doesn't need.

**Store:** `src/lib/networking.ts`, one `useSyncExternalStore` + `localStorage` key (`dreamari-networking`), same idiom as `picks.ts`/`resume.ts`. Both "sides" of the demo share this one browser, same limitation as every other prototype store.

**Files:** `src/lib/networking.ts` (new), `src/components/connect/networking/pov.tsx` (new), `src/components/connect/networking/Conversation.tsx` (new), `src/components/connect/networking/StudentMessaging.tsx` (new), `src/components/connect/networking/ProRequestsPanel.tsx` (new), `src/components/connect/ProProfile.tsx` (POV chip + Message panel), `src/components/connect/ProDashboard.tsx` (new Messaging tab).

**Validation.** `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` clean; `npx eslint` clean on every touched/new file. Verified live with Playwright at 1366x820 and 390x844: College POV toggle, Message gated by Follow, sending one request, the waiting state and allowance line, the pro-side request list with full context, Accept, and the resulting conversation -- on both the live student's own (empty) activity and the two seeded students' activity. No console errors either breakpoint.

**Left for a follow-up, not built here:** notifications for "request accepted"/"new request waiting" (the app's existing notification feed, `notificationsData.ts`, isn't wired to this store yet); a way to change an already-sent pending request; and `ConnectExperience.tsx`'s own People tab / role switch don't surface a "Messages" entry point yet -- today the only way into this feature is the pro profile's own College toggle. A next step would add a small unread/pending indicator to the existing bell or People tab once that file is free to edit (another session owned it during this one).

## 2026-09-28 · Connect Feed

**Why.** Joshua's 30-person focus group: "when a student follows a professional, it is not obvious what happens next." Followed pros' new answers and posts were buried at the bottom of People (`NewFromFollowing`, capped at 4) or behind Following, several taps deep, with no ranking against anything else worth seeing.

**What.** Feed is now Connect's first tab and default landing (`Feed | Communities | Mentorship | People | Events`, `LANDING_TABS`/`LANDING_TAB_NAMES` in `ConnectExperience.tsx`; `/connect` with no `?tab=` now opens Feed instead of Communities -- `queryToView`, the initial `useState`, `goBack`'s empty-stack fallback, and the role switcher's student pick all updated together so nothing silently falls back to the old default). One continuous, personalised feed, not a For You/Following split: real Answers and Posts from `data.ts`, ranked and mixed together.

**Ranking** (`src/components/connect/feed/rankFeed.ts`, a pure function, no React/DOM): scores every answered question and every insight post on one scale -- followed pros first, then pros the student demonstrably engages with (liked or saved their content) even unfollowed, then relevance to the student's own worlds/joined communities, then plain popularity (the seed data's `helpful` count) and recency as tie-breakers. Cold start (no follows, no Top 3 yet) still produces a full, real order from the last two factors alone, so a new student never sees an empty feed.

**Design, second pass same day (direct correction after the first ship):** the first version put a quiet "why this is here" reason label on every card ("You follow Tiana", "Popular in Tech & Engineering"); direct feedback -- "Joshua's notes never asked for it; social feeds don't label posts from people you follow" -- replaced it with an actual social-feed read (Instagram home / LinkedIn), one centred column (max 600px), one post per row: an author row (avatar, name, verified mark, company, relative time), a quiet "Answered/Posted in {world}" line to the board (tappable, unless that board no longer exists, in which case it's plain text), the content as the hero (an answer previews its own question first, a post leads with its title, clamped ~5 lines with "more"), then helpful/comments/save/share. The *only* label kept is "Suggested for you" plus an inline Follow, and only on a post from a pro the student doesn't follow yet -- pressing it fires the same Follow confirmation toast as everywhere else and the label disappears from that post immediately (it's derived from live follow state, not cached).

**Contrast, direct correction:** the first pass's card blended into the page background; posts now sit on `var(--card)` with a real `var(--border)` and a soft shadow, tokens that already carry their own light/dark values, checked in both.

**Interactions:** Helpful/Save are optimistic local toggles (`cardProps`, same store as every other Connect surface); Share reuses `nav.share` (clipboard copy + its existing confirmation); tapping anywhere on a post opens the original board discussion (`nav.openThread`/`openInsight`) except the controls layered above that tap target (same layered-button trick `QuestionCard`/`InsightCard` already use, not `stopPropagation` everywhere). Zero engagement counts hide the number and keep just the icon (`HelpfulPill` and the comments count both do this now, app-wide -- a "0" read as noise, not information); the real count is still in each control's aria-label.

**Infinite-feel and states:** batches of 6 reveal via an IntersectionObserver sentinel (`useFeedSentinel`, the same technique as flow-lab's `useRevealCount`, kept local rather than importing across feature areas), with a short deliberate pause and a post-shaped `Shimmer` skeleton so the loading state is actually visible, and "You're all caught up" plus a "Discover more people" CTA at the real end (92 items in the seed data). Already-rendered rows never reorder under the student's thumb when they follow someone; a newly-followed pro's other content can only rise into the *next* batch, drawn from a freshly recomputed ranking. A student following no one gets a light "Follow a few professionals to personalise your feed" card above a still-full, recommendation-only feed. A "New" pill marks anything posted within the last 3 hours, but only on the very first time this browser tab opens the feed this session (`sessionStorage`, `dm-connect-feed-visited`) -- an honest approximation given the seed data has no real per-item timestamp to diff against an actual last-visit time. Loading/error/empty/offline go through `SurfaceState id={63}` (a new id; 1-62 were already claimed elsewhere in the app).

**Follow's immediate payoff:** the focus group's other direct ask. `toggleFollow` in `ConnectExperience.tsx` is the one place every Follow control in Connect (profile, People, a board's Pros tab, the feed) ultimately calls, so the confirmation lives there once: a real `Toast` (not just the existing sr-only banner), "Following {first name}. New answers and posts from {first name} will now appear in your feed." Only on following, never on unfollow; pronoun-free since `Pro` has no pronoun field.

**People tab:** removed "New from people you follow" (`NewFromFollowing` in `PeopleTab.tsx`) now that the same content, ranked and mixed with recommendations, is Connect's own first tab -- kept Search professionals, Active People to Follow, Browse by Industry. `NewFromFollowing` itself is untouched (Notifications and Your Activity still use it).

**Cross-browser fix, found in review:** `TopTabs`' 4-tab pill became 5 tabs (`grid-cols-5`); at a phone width "Communities"/"Mentorship" no longer fit and painted over the next tab (a grid item won't shrink below its content's width by default, and the button had no `min-w-0`/`overflow-hidden`/truncation). Fixed with `min-w-0 overflow-hidden` on each tab button, a truncating `<span>` around the label, and a smaller label size below `sm:`.

**Files:** `src/components/connect/feed/rankFeed.ts` (new), `src/components/connect/ConnectExperience.tsx` (Feed tab, `FeedTab`/`FeedPostRow`/`FeedPostSkeleton`/`useFeedSentinel`, the Follow toast, `TopTabs` fix, `HelpfulPill`'s zero-count fix), `src/components/connect/PeopleTab.tsx` (removed the one usage), `src/lib/surfaceStates.ts` (surface 63).

Screenshots: `feed-desktop.png`, `feed-phone.png`, `feed-light.png`, `follow-toast.png` in this session's scratchpad.

A post whose board no longer exists renders its context line as plain text instead of a link, exercised by code review only (today's seed data has no such orphan to click through live).

### Follow-up (same day): withdraw + real notifications

Three more pieces the Harvard-team spec asked for, built the same session:

**Withdraw a pending request.** `withdrawRequest(id)` in `src/lib/networking.ts` removes the request and, if it was sent in the current allowance week, refunds the slot (`used` decremented) so the student can send a new one right away. `StudentMessaging.tsx`'s pending state now shows a quiet "Withdraw request" link; clicking it swaps in an inline "Withdraw this request? You'll get the slot back." confirm with "Yes, withdraw" / "Never mind" -- no native `confirm()` dialog anywhere in the flow.

**Wired into the app's real notifications**, not a parallel system. `networkingNotifications(store)` (`src/lib/networking.ts`) computes rows straight from the live store every render -- a request moving from pending to accepted simply stops producing one row and starts producing another, so there's never a stale duplicate to clean up:
- Student-facing: "**Amara** accepted your request. Say hello!" (opens the conversation) and, on decline, "**Amara** isn't taking requests right now. Ask in Community instead." (opens the pro's community board) -- positive framing, no rejection wording.
- Pro-facing: "New request from Jordan, sophomore interested in Investment Banking" (opens the dashboard's Messaging tab).
- Either direction: the newest unread message in an accepted thread produces its own "sent you a message" row.

Read/unread reuses the app's existing inbox (`src/lib/inbox.ts`) rather than a second tracked-state store: every dynamic row gets a stable id (`net-accepted-<reqId>`, `net-declined-<reqId>`, `net-newreq-<reqId>`, `net-msg-<reqId>-<messageAt>`), and opening one from the bell marks it read the same way any other notification does (`markNotificationRead`). `Inbox.tsx`'s `useVisibleNotifications` now merges `networkingNotifications()` with the static `NOTIFICATIONS` array each render; a new `"message"` icon (`MessagesSquare`) was added to `notificationsData.ts`'s icon union and `Inbox.tsx`'s icon map for the pro-facing rows, which have no avatar (a generated student identity, not a static image).

**`useNetworkingUnread(as, proId?)`** and **`messagesHref(as, proId?)`**, both exported from `src/lib/networking.ts` for whoever wires a "Messages" entry point into Connect's own nav later (not built here -- `ConnectExperience.tsx`/`PeopleTab.tsx` were owned by another session this round):
- `useNetworkingUnread("pro", proId?)` = pending requests for that pro + unread student messages in its accepted threads (omit `proId` to sum across every pro).
- `useNetworkingUnread("student", proId?)` = unread accepts/declines + unread pro messages for the live student's own requests.
- Both read the identical `net-*` ids the bell already tracks, so this count and the bell's badge can never drift apart.
- `messagesHref("student", proId?)` -> the pro's profile in College POV (`?pov=college`); `messagesHref("pro", proId?)` -> that pro's dashboard, Messaging tab (`?net=messages`, read by `ProDashboard.tsx` on mount to preselect the tab).

**Files touched (in addition to the original list):** `src/lib/networking.ts` (withdraw, notifications, unread hook, href helper), `src/lib/inbox.ts` (read only, no changes needed -- its existing `read`/`markNotificationRead` were reused as-is), `src/components/app/Inbox.tsx`, `src/components/app/notificationsData.ts`, `src/components/connect/networking/StudentMessaging.tsx` (withdraw UI), `src/components/connect/ProDashboard.tsx` (`?net=messages` deep link).

**Validation.** `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` clean; `npx eslint` clean on every touched file (one `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` finding in the new `ProDashboard.tsx` URL-restore effect, resolved with the same disable-comment convention `ConnectExperience.tsx`'s own view-restore effect already uses). Verified live with Playwright: withdrew a pending request (inline confirm, no native dialog, allowance correctly back to 3 of 3), the pro-facing "New request from Maya Sinclair..." notification appears in the bell from the seeded data with no action needed, clicking it deep-links to the Messaging tab, accepting a live request produces "Amara accepted your request. Say hello!" for the student with the bell's unread count incrementing on accept and decrementing after the notification is opened, and an accepted seeded thread's initial message surfaces as "Diego Fields sent you a message" on the pro side (the same "unread message in an accepted conversation" path, exercised incidentally). No console errors, no native dialogs, in either scenario.

## 2026-09-28 (later still) · Connect Feed, final layout and value-adds; Insights renamed to Posts app-wide

**Why.** Same-day iteration on the Connect Feed above, driven by direct review: the first ship's single centred column "looked a little weird and empty" on a wide page, the information hierarchy inside each card wasn't clear against Quora/Reddit/LinkedIn/Instagram conventions, the College networking Messages entry point (built by the parallel networking session) was easy to lose, and a separate direct ask simplified "Insights" to "Posts" everywhere in Connect's own vocabulary.

**Layout, after three passes.** A three-column LinkedIn-style layout (profile/communities rail + feed + recommendations rail) was tried, then a two-column version, then explicitly pulled back: "avoid clutter and competing focus." What shipped: one feed column, full width inside Connect's own content column (no extra max-width wrapper of its own, so its edges match the CONNECT title and tab bar exactly), with reading text capped at `max-w-[70ch]` inside each card so a wide card's paragraph still reads as a column. At `xl` (>=1280px) one slim sticky right rail carries "People you might like" only (3-4 pros: avatar, name + verified, "{org} · {world}" reason line, Follow -- following one removes them from the recommendation list so the next one takes their place, no extra code needed). Below `xl`, the same recommendation list appears instead as a horizontal "People you might like" strip woven into the feed every 5 posts (`ProStrip`/`MiniProCard`, shared with the rail). The "Ask professionals a question" composer stays at the very top; the orphan "Your feed" heading is gone for good.

**Card hierarchy, redone to forum/feed convention (direct correction: "the information hierarchy in the cards isn't clear").** Answer cards follow Quora's own order: an eyebrow (board dot + "{world} · {time}", "Suggested · " prefix and a Follow button on the right when not yet followed, smallest/quietest text), the question itself as the card's one emphasized element (17px/600), a compact attribution row (28px avatar, "{name} ✓ · {role} at {company}"), the answer body in regular weight (not bold) clamped to 4 lines with "Read more", then a footer. Post cards follow LinkedIn's own order instead: a 40px author row (name ✓, "{role} · {time} · in {world}" muted, the board folded in rather than a separate line), the post's own title folded into the body's opening line (posts have no separate headline slot, so nothing here competes with the author's name), the body clamped to 5 lines, then the same footer. The footer spreads a career chip (left, only when confident) against the action cluster (right): Helpful, comments, Ask a follow-up, Save, Share, and a small overflow menu -- spread across the card's full width instead of stacked.

**Five value-adds, direct ask:**
1. **Inline event card.** When a followed pro's real employer appears in a real Upcoming event board's own `orgs` list *and* that board has an actual date (several seeded Upcoming boards only carry a "First event to be announced" placeholder, which read as nonsense next to "is live" -- QA finding, fixed by requiring a real date), one card surfaces near the top of the feed: "{first name} is live {date} · {event name}", a Remind me toggle (confirmation toast, `FeedEventCard`), tapping opens the event through the same joined/code gate the Events tab's own cards use. At most one, computed once, never per batch.
2. **Ask a follow-up.** A quiet action in every answer/post's footer (`Reply` icon) that opens the same `AskSheet` used by the composer, now pre-addressed: `AskSheet` gained optional `initialBoardId`/`initialText` props, and `ConnectNav` gained `askFollowUp(boardId, proName)`, which seeds the sheet with that answer's board and the draft "Following up on {name}'s answer: ", fully still editable.
3. **Save -> Career Locker.** A new small store, `src/lib/connectSaves.ts` (same `useSyncExternalStore`/localStorage idiom as every other `src/lib` store), deliberately additive rather than a rewrite of Connect's existing in-memory `saves` state (which still drives every other Save button in Connect unchanged). The Feed's own Save button also writes through to this store and shows "Saved to your Career Locker." once per save. Profile's Locker (`ProfileExperience.tsx`) gained a fifth shelf, "From Connect" (`ConnectSavesShelf`), a plain list of saved answers/posts that link back to the original Connect discussion -- kept intentionally minimal (no per-career grouping) since not every saved item has a confident career match; noted here as a real next step if wanted.
4. **Related career chip.** `careerChipFor(pro)`: the pro's own `field` (e.g. "Investment Banking") checked for an *exact* title match in the app's career catalog, confirmed to have a real Career Detail profile (`careerProfile`), before it earns a chip linking to `/career/<slug>`. No fuzzy fallback -- a post either clearly is about one cataloged career or gets no chip (direct ask: "skip if no confident match"), which is why most posts in the seed data don't show one.
5. **See less like this.** A minimal one-item overflow menu (`MoreMenu`, IconTip "More") that hides that one post in place with an inline "Hidden. Undo" row (nothing else on screen jumps), and demotes its pro and board for the rest of the session (`rankFeed`'s new optional `demotedProIds`/`demotedBoardIds`, subtracted from score after every other factor -- a real follow still can't be fully buried by one demotion). Undo restores only that one post; the session-wide demotion is a separate, longer-lived signal and isn't reversed by Undo.

**Global surfacing, three direct corrections in a row:**
- The High School/College demo switch (`networking/pov.tsx`, unchanged) was only reachable from a pro's own profile. `PovChip` now also renders in Connect's own header, beside the existing "Demo" toggle -- same shared module-level state, so both stay in sync.
- The Connect welcome splash's third row ("Volunteers can't follow or privately message students") now reads "Students can message volunteers who accept their request" in the College POV specifically (`PeopleWelcome` passes a `scene` override to the shared `WelcomeSplash`); High School keeps today's line.
- The Messages entry point moved twice: first into Connect's own header (next to the tabs), then out to the **app's global header** next to the notification bell (direct ask: "like Instagram/TikTok DMs"), so it's reachable from Home too, not just Connect. `MessagesButton` (new, `src/components/app/Inbox.tsx`, exported) reuses `NavIconButton` exactly (same size/style/hover/badge as the bell) and reads `?as=`/`?dashboard=` the same way Connect's own role switch does, so it works from any page: student side uses `useNetworkingUnread("student")` and `messagesHref("student", proId)` (most-recently-active conversation, since there's no dedicated inbox list yet), pro side (`?as=pro`) uses `useNetworkingUnread("pro", dashboardProId)` and `messagesHref("pro", dashboardProId)`. Shown in the College POV, or once the student already has a real request/conversation even if the POV reset to High School on reload; never otherwise. Rendered in both `DesktopNavigation` and `HeaderActions` (mobile), right before `NotificationsButton` in each.

**"Insights" renamed to "Posts," app-wide (direct ask: "no insights anywhere, everything is just called posts").** Display text only -- every id, route param (`?insight=`, `?filter=insights`), `kind`/`type` discriminant (`"insight"`), and component/type name (`Insight`, `InsightCard`, `openInsight`, etc.) is untouched, so nothing that reads or links by id broke. Changed: aria-labels and screen-reader text ("Open post", "Report this post", "Previous/Next post", the insight-carousel's "Posts" tablist label), the post-thread page's "Post" eyebrow (was "Professional insight"), a locker onboarding line, a seeded peer reply that self-referentially said "insight" ("every single post on this app" now), and the AT&T board's own share-sheet and year-round-prompt copy (`attData.ts` + its `v1` twin: "Share post"/"Share a post", `INSIGHTS_SECTION` title "Professional Posts"). One real naming conflict surfaced: the AT&T Event board's own tab list already had a separate "Posts" tab (the event account's official/recap posts) sitting alongside the professional-insights tab -- renaming both to "Posts" would have collided, so the professional one became "Pro posts" instead, noted inline. Two things were deliberately left alone as unrelated to this feature: "Insight Day" / "Early Insights Program" (real recruiting-program terms in the seed data, e.g. an actual Morgan Stanley program name) and the Play simulation's own "market insight" dialogue (`component-lab/sections/game/PlayInteractions.tsx`) -- neither is Connect's Insight/Post type. Counselor Dashboard, marketing pages, and `ib-level-*.ts` untouched, per instruction (Counselor's own "Insights" is analytics, a different word for a different thing). `grep -rniE '\binsights?\b' src` still returns ~307 hits; all remaining ones were checked by hand and are ids, route params, `kind`/`type` values, component names, or comments -- no remaining user-facing string says "insight."

## 2026-09-29 · Career simulation art pipeline: automatic, one manifest per career

**Why.** Usman: "From the backend point of view, the game works, but the post processing... like generating and positioning graphics introduces a manual process, that is not easy to manage and scale." The user: "build and do whatever it takes to help Usman so he has no more excuses", "something he can use to scale for every new career simulation", then, on the first plan's drag-to-position tool: "that seems like a manual process... I want it to be automated so we don't have to manually do anything. We have 900+ careers." Image and sprite prompts run in Codex (Claude cannot generate images), so the pipeline starts after Codex.

**What changed.**
- **Art is data.** `src/components/play/art/<career>.json` (schema `career-art.schema.json`, types `types.ts`, list `index.ts`) holds a career's rooms (src, alt, role, focal, mobileFocal, slots, locked), cast (default, tiers, face, voicePitch), sprite ratios and beat to room routing. IB and RN were exported from the old code tables, so the game is unchanged; `locations.ts`, `expressions.ts` and `VOICE_PITCH` in `SimulationPlayer.tsx` now only read the manifests.
- **`scripts/play-art/play-art.mjs`** (sharp): `new-career`, `prompts` (Codex prompt pack from cast.json and rooms.json), `process` (chroma key, despill, despeckle, trim, standard 1024x2048 canvas, webp, face chips, plates, heroes, ratios, cast wiring), `place` (focal points computed from the plate: clearest standing column by edge density, solved through the object-cover math; runs inside `process`), `qa` (head/face geometry at five viewports, no screenshots), `validate`, `measure`. npm: `art:new|prompts|process|place|qa|validate|route`.
- **`scripts/play-beats/map-beats.mjs`**: routes every beat of a level to a room. Claude engine (API, default `claude-sonnet-5`) with the written house style; offline rules fallback.
- **`/play-tools/scene-review`**: read-only QA page, every room at 390x844, 768x1024, 1440x900, 1920x1080 and 2560x1080 with the player's own math (`src/components/play/scenePlacement.ts`, now shared by the player), automatic flags and a Flagged-only toggle.
- **Guide**: `docs/handoff/play-sop/08-new-career-art-pipeline.md` (also sent to Usman as a Google Doc); SOP README and intake template point at the manifest.

**Validation.** tsc and eslint clean. Player refactor: 50 sprite positions on both games at 390x844 and 1440x900 identical before and after (top/height 0px). Review page frames match the player within 0.00006 of frame height. `measure`: every stored ratio equals the real file. Synthetic green-screen career end to end: clean key, correct framing, chips centred, TODO alt fails QA. Beat routing, blind (the model saw only the prompt): 72 of 113 shipped beats match the hand routing (64%), from 47% before the house style was written down; offline rules 46%. Auto placement vs hand tuning: plain rooms within 0.02 to 0.09; divergence only where hand tuning encoded story ("never over the bed") or the plate was not made to the clear-centre standard (IB trading floor), and `place` flags those itself.

**Findings.** All ten shipped RN sprites carry green edge spill (53 to 60% of edge pixels), caught by `validate`. RN's lobby plate is routed to no beat.

**Left open.** `cobalt-trading-floor-sunset` in `investment-banking.json` still lacks `"locked": true` and `"role": "work-floor"` (a subagent's edit to it was refused by the permission classifier; not retried). The shared-room-library idea for 900 careers is a proposal for Joshua and Chandu, not built. The review page's dialogue-box zone is modelled from the one-line card.

**Why.** Joshua: "too many controls, labels, and decisions visible at once... Instagram reveals tools progressively"; "a volunteer should create something attractive in under a minute without feeling like they are using a design program"; plus a curated Unsplash set for "beautiful photography + strong typography + a short professional insight", Bible-app verse cards as the reference, text "in the cleanest area of the image", and a watermark "like Gemini does" so reposts drive traffic back. Chandu: "use Instagram's UI, not a huge form and endless menus", keep gradients and patterns too, "keep our background and functionality, enable undo, keep the vector stuff, remove the emoji sticker", "allow alignment controls, make the default auto", "add a Dreamari brandmark to a corner... customizable if it clashes".

**What changed.**
- **`connect/PostComposer.tsx`, rewritten.**
  - The header has Close, a **Text post | Graphic post** switch, and Share or Next.
  - **Text post** is a title and the words only. Ideas fold under "Need an idea?".
  - **Graphic post** is the canvas, filling the screen, with Instagram's bottom toolbar of four icons: Background, Text, Effects, Mark. Tapping one slides up only its choices; tapping it again, or the canvas, closes them. Undo, Redo and a small Surprise me (shuffle) sit on the canvas, with Cmd/Ctrl+Z as well. Tapping the words edits them. Next goes to the caption.
  - **Caption** shows a thumbnail, the title and words, and a **Share to** community row, which Joshua asked for as "create once, select the relevant community". `ProDashboard` now publishes to the chosen board.

  - `scripts/career-photos/graphic-photos.mjs` measures each photo: the calmest band for the words, light or dark ink, and the calmest corner for the mark. Per-corner ink was then added so the mark contrasts in any corner.
  - Placement is Auto by default: words in the measured band, left-aligned like the Bible app, and the mark in the measured corner. Text offers Auto plus left, centre, right and top, middle, bottom; Mark offers Auto plus four corners.
- **`InsightGraphicView`**: graphics are now 4:5 portrait (Instagram's post shape, so they repost cleanly), capped at 440px in feeds. The volunteer's role, company and name sit just above the words, the way "Verse of the Day / 1 Peter 4:8" does. The DREAMARI mark (logo plus wordmark) is on every graphic.
- **`GraphicDesigner` removed**: the old all-options panel.

**Validation.** tsc and eslint clean. Browser at desktop and 375: Text and Graphic modes; Background, Text and Mark trays; Undo enabled after a change; Next to caption; Share publishes to the volunteer's Posts as a 440x550 graphic; the student Feed's graphics render 4:5 with the mark. No console errors.

**Same evening, second pass** (Chandu, with Instagram story screenshots: "can text editing be inline like on the post itself?"; "editing should be inline in the preview itself, just a hint to tap the preview"; "pick a tab from the bottom > its menu opens as a side-scrollable strip overlaid at the bottom of the preview > select"; "get rid of scenes and paper from the background menu").

  - **Text:** fonts, each name in its own face, then Auto, align left, centre and right, top, middle and bottom, No box, Highlight or Card, CAPS, and colour (Auto colour plus 8 swatches; new `InsightGraphic.color`).
  - **Background:** group chips, then thumbnails.
  - **Effects:** effect chips.
  - **Mark:** a strip of corners, plus the four corners as tap targets on the preview itself.

**Third pass** (Chandu: "reduce the number of things at once for text... research the best and simplest UI"; "use logos instead of typing out company names"; "let's see if the profile picture can be brought back"; then "look at Apple Music and Spotify sharing templates").
